'''Sergio Ramos García''' ({{IPA|es|ˈseɾxjo ˈramos ɣaɾˈθi.a}};{{efn-ua|In isolation, ''Ramos'' and ''García'' are pronounced {{IPA|es|ˈramos|}} and {{IPA|es|ɡaɾˈθi.a|}} respectively.}} born 30 March 1986) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]]. Widely regarded as one of the greatest centre-backs of all time, he is known for his aerial abilities, physicality, leadership, and goalscoring abilities, having scored more than 100 goals for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hepburn |first=Daniel |date=9 April 2020 |title=Fans have ranked the 50 best defenders in football history |url=https://www.givemesport.com/football-fans-rank-the-50-greatest-defenders-in-football-history/ |access-date=10 February 2026 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250831140452/https://www.givemesport.com/football-fans-rank-the-50-greatest-defenders-in-football-history/ |archive-date=31 August 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=10 greatest defenders of all time{{!}} All Football |url=https://m.allfootballapp.com/news/All/10-greatest-defenders-of-all-time/2760135 |access-date=10 February 2026 |website=AllfootballOfficial |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260128063252/https://m.allfootballapp.com/news/All/10-greatest-defenders-of-all-time/2760135 |archive-date=28 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 December 2024 |title=The 50 Best Defenders in Soccer History—Ranked |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/ranking-the-50-best-soccer-defenders-of-all-time |access-date=10 February 2026 |website=SI |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627054744/https://www.si.com/soccer/ranking-the-50-best-soccer-defenders-of-all-time |archive-date=27 June 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In addition, he is one of the few players to have made [[List of men's footballers with 1,000 or more official appearances|over 1,050 career appearances]].

Born in [[Camas, Seville|Camas]] in the Spanish [[province of Seville]], Ramos played in [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]'s youth academy and spent two seasons with the senior team, before moving to Real Madrid in the summer of 2005. He went on to become a mainstay for the club, winning 22 major honours, including five [[La Liga]] titles and four [[UEFA Champions League]] titles. He was vital to all of the Champions League winning campaigns, as he was named in the competition's Team of the Season each time. Out of contract with Real Madrid, he signed for Ligue 1 club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in July 2021, spending two seasons at the club and winning [[Ligue 1]] twice, before returning to Sevilla for one season. After leaving Sevilla, Ramos joined [[Liga MX]] side [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]], where he captained the team and played in the inaugural edition of the expanded [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].

Internationally, Ramos represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] from 2005 to 2021, playing at four [[FIFA World Cup]]s  (winning the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 edition]]) and three [[UEFA European Championship]]s (winning titles in [[UEFA Euro 2008|2008]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012|2012]]). With 180 caps earned across sixteen years, he is the nation's [[Spain national football team#Most capped players|record appearance holder]].

==Club career==
===Sevilla===
Born in [[Camas, Seville|Camas]], [[province of Seville]], Andalusia,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/05/31/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1401520987.html|title=Sergio Ramos, el origen|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=31 May 2014|access-date=27 May 2019|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527022429/https://www.marca.com/2014/05/31/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1401520987.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos started playing at Camas CF by age six,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sergioramos.com/en/primera-ficha-oficial-en-la-federacion-andaluza-de-futbol/ |title=Kicking a ball in Camas for the first time |website=sergioramos.com |access-date=23 November 2020 |archive-date=29 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429182054/https://www.sergioramos.com/en/primera-ficha-oficial-en-la-federacion-andaluza-de-futbol/ |url-status=live }}</ref> then he began his career at local side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], emerging through the club's youth system alongside [[Jesús Navas]] and [[Antonio Puerta]]. He made his first-team and [[La Liga]] debut on 1 February 2004, coming on as a 64th-minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Paco Gallardo]] in a 0–1 away loss against [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Deportivo no pierde las esperanzas|trans-title=Deportivo don't lose hope|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/cronica?id=135850|access-date=7 July 2015|publisher=ESPN|date=1 February 2004|language=es|archive-date=7 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707082846/http://espndeportes.espn.go.com/futbol/cronica?id=135850|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the 2004–05 season, Ramos appeared in 41 games as Sevilla finished sixth and qualified to the [[2005–06 UEFA Cup]], scoring in home fixtures against [[Real Sociedad]] (2–1)<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/163917?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716023941/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/163917?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 July 2012|title=FC Sevilla 2–1 Real Sociedad|publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]]|date=26 September 2004|access-date=1 June 2012}}</ref> and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (2–2).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/179114?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120728224057/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/179114?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 July 2012|title=FC Sevilla 2–2 Real Madrid|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=14 May 2005|access-date=1 June 2012}}</ref> In the [[2004–05 UEFA Cup]], he scored his first continental goal, heading to conclude a 2–0 win over [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramon Sánchez Pizjuán]] in the [[2004–05 UEFA Cup first round|first round]] (4–1 aggregate).<ref>{{cite news|title=SEVILLA FC 2 – CD NACIONAL DE MADEIRA 0|url=http://www.sevillacf.com/cronicasdeeuropa/sevilla2nacionalmadeira0.htm|access-date=24 March 2016|date=16 September 2004|language=es|archive-date=13 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313145533/http://www.sevillacf.com/cronicasdeeuropa/sevilla2nacionalmadeira0.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
====2005–09: Record transfer and early days====
[[File:Sergio Ramos 10mar2007.jpg|thumb|190px|Ramos playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in March 2007]]

In the summer of 2005, Ramos was purchased by Real Madrid for €27&nbsp;million, a record for a Spanish defender.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thinkspain.com/news-spain/9451/sergio-ramos-joins-real-madrid-for-27-million|title=Sergio Ramos joins Real Madrid for €27&nbsp;million|publisher=Think Spain|date=1 September 2005|access-date=19 November 2010|archive-date=17 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717045949/http://www.thinkspain.com/news-spain/9451/sergio-ramos-joins-real-madrid-for-27-million|url-status=live}}</ref> He was the only Spanish player brought in during [[Florentino Pérez]]'s first stint as Real Madrid’s president.

At the club, Ramos was assigned the number 4 shirt, previously worn by [[Fernando Hierro]]. On 6 December 2005 he netted his first goal for the ''Meringues'', in a 2–1 [[UEFA Champions League]] [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|group stage loss]] at [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188827&cc=5739|title=Olympiakos 2–1 Real Madrid: Second-string|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=6 December 2005|access-date=17 May 2011|archive-date=25 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025001802/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=188827&cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref>

During his first seasons, Ramos played as centre back, being also used as an emergency [[defensive midfielder]] on occasion. However, with the arrival of [[Christoph Metzelder]] and [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] in the [[2007–08 Real Madrid CF season|2007–08 season]], he was again relocated to right back. In his first four seasons at Real Madrid, Ramos displayed a goalscoring instinct unusual to many defenders, netting more than 20 goals overall. He also received the first nine of his 24 red cards for the club, including four in [[2005–06 Real Madrid CF season|his debut season]]. His first red card came after two bookable offences in a 1–0 away loss to [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] on 18 September 2005.<ref name=retrospective>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/23/sergio-ramos-19-real-madrid-red-cards|title=Sergio Ramos and his 21 Real Madrid red cards: a retrospective|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=4 April 2016|access-date=5 April 2016|archive-date=10 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200410093408/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/23/sergio-ramos-19-real-madrid-red-cards|url-status=live}}</ref>

During the [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07 season]], Ramos scored five goals, including one in a 3–3 ''[[El Clásico]]'' draw with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], as Real Madrid won a record 30th [[List of Spanish football champions|league title]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/sergio-ramos-the-highest-scoring-defender-in-the-liga-since-2009|title=Sergio Ramos, the highest-scoring defender in the Liga since 2009|date=6 September 2009|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=5 April 2016|archive-date=29 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729014236/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/09/sergio-ramos-the-highest-scoring-defender-in-the-liga-since-2009|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 May 2008, he assisted [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] in the [[Last-minute goal|89th minute]] against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] in an eventual 2–1 away win, the match that sealed the club's 31st league championship. On the final day of the season, he scored twice in a 5–2 home win against already relegated [[Levante UD|Levante]]: one through a header, and another an individual effort; these goals taking his league tally for the [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08 season]] to five.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/226702?cc=5739|title=Real Madrid 5–2 Levante|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=18 May 2008|access-date=1 June 2012|archive-date=21 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621143412/http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?cc=5739&id=226702|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 24 August 2008, Ramos scored in the [[2008 Supercopa de España]] second leg against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], making the score 2–1 in an eventual 4–2 and 6–5 aggregate win. The victory came despite Real Madrid playing with only nine men for a long period of time after [[Rafael van der Vaart]] and [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] were sent off. Although Ramos experienced a slight dip in form during the early part of the [[2008–09 Real Madrid CF season|2008–09 season]], he returned to his best and on 11 January 2009, scoring an acrobatic volley in a 3–0 triumph at [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/253068?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720023848/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/253068?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 July 2012|title=Mallorca 0–3 Real Madrid|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=11 January 2009|access-date=1 June 2012}}</ref> He continued his scoring run the following week in a 3–1 [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|home]] win against Osasuna.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/252960?cc=5739|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Osasuna|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=18 January 2009|access-date=1 June 2012|archive-date=2 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102022925/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/252960?cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ramos was named in both [[FIFA]] and [[UEFA]]'s 2008 ''Team of the Year'', adding the FIFPro Team of the Year 2007–08 accolade. He also finished 21st in the European Player of the Year nomination for 2008.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2010/08/23/2083595/chelsea-readying-mammoth-40-million-swoop-for-real-madrid Chelsea readying mammoth €40 million swoop for Real Madrid defender Sergio Ramos] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203051900/https://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2010/08/23/2083595/chelsea-readying-mammoth-40-million-swoop-for-real-madrid |date=3 February 2022 }}; Goal.com, 23 August 2010</ref>

====2009–14: Breakout and team mainstay====
At the start of the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]], Ramos was appointed as one of Real Madrid's four captains. Because Pepe had suffered a serious knee injury during this campaign, Ramos was often deployed as central defender. He scored four goals in 33 league matches; and, on 21 February 2010 he played his 200th official match for ''Los Blancos'' against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] (150 in the first division). Despite these personal highlights, Real Madrid finished the campaign without picking up any silverware.

[[File:Control de Sergio Ramos.jpg|thumb|right|190px|Ramos in action for Real Madrid in October 2010.]]

In Real Madrid's 5–0 loss at Barcelona on 29 November 2010, Ramos was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] after kicking [[Lionel Messi]] from behind, then pushing [[Carles Puyol]] in the ensuing melée.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301858&cc=5739|title=Exquisite Barca crush Real|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=29 November 2010|access-date=29 November 2010|archive-date=12 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121112025154/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301858&cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref> After this ejection, he equalled [[Fernando Hierro]]'s previous record of ten red cards at the club, despite having played in 264 fewer games.<ref>[http://www.resultados-futbol.com/noticia/sergio-ramos-ya-ha-igualado-diez-tarjetas-rojas-fernando-hierro Sergio Ramos ya ha igualado las diez tarjetas rojas de Fernando Hierro (Sergio Ramos equals Fernando Hierro's record of ten red cards)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203051904/https://www.resultados-futbol.com/noticia/sergio-ramos-ya-ha-igualado-diez-tarjetas-rojas-fernando-hierro |date=3 February 2022 }}; Resultados-Futbol {{in lang|es}}</ref> On 20 April 2011, Ramos started in [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|the season]]'s [[Copa del Rey]] [[2011 Copa del Rey Final|final]], a 1–0 win against Barcelona in [[Valencia]]. In the subsequent victory procession, while celebrating on the top of the club's bus, he accidentally lost hold of the cup, which fell under the wheels of the vehicle; the trophy was dented as a result.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/sportvideo/footballvideo/8465404/Real-Madrids-Sergio-Ramos-drops-Copa-del-Rey-trophy-off-bus.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110423173332/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/sportvideo/footballvideo/8465404/Real-Madrids-Sergio-Ramos-drops-Copa-del-Rey-trophy-off-bus.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 April 2011|title=Real Madrid's Sergio Ramos drops Copa del Rey trophy off bus|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=21 April 2011|access-date=21 April 2011}}</ref>

On 12 July 2011, Ramos extended his contract with Real Madrid until 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/933989/pepesergio-ramos-pen-real-madrid-contract-extensions|title=Pepe, Ramos extend Real contracts|publisher=espnfc.com|date=12 July 2011|access-date=27 July 2011|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330181859/http://www.espnfc.com/story/933989/pepesergio-ramos-pen-real-madrid-contract-extensions|url-status=live}}</ref> The following 25 April, in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Semi-finals|Champions League semi-finals' second leg]] against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], he missed his [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] attempt as Real Madrid lost 3–1;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d7dd2ce94cf-82e59fa2db44-1000--spot-on-bayern-edge-madrid-thriller-to-reach-final/|title=Spot-on Bayern edge Madrid thriller to reach final|publisher=UEFA|date=25 April 2012|access-date=30 April 2012|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331044135/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2012/matches/round=2000266/match=2007691/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> the league campaign ended with them winning, with a record 100 points, after a four-year wait and he was the player with most balls recovered in his team, third overall.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://omgghana.com/real-madrids-sergio-ramos-named-king-of-steals/|title=Real Madrid's Sergio Ramos Named 'King of Steals'|publisher=omgghana.com|date=11 July 2012|access-date=27 July 2012|archive-date=26 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141226224327/http://omgghana.com/real-madrids-sergio-ramos-named-king-of-steals/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 9 January 2013, Ramos was sent off for a second [[Penalty card#Yellow card|bookable offense]] midway through the second half of an eventual 4–0 home win over [[Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] in the [[2012–13 Copa del Rey]]. He subsequently received a four-match suspension, after it was revealed he also insulted [[Referee (association football)|referee]] Miguel Ángel Ayza Gámez.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1294563/real-madrid%27s-ramos-handed-five-match-ban?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216035827/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1294563/real-madrid's-ramos-handed-five-match-ban?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 February 2013|title=Ramos handed five-match ban|publisher=ESPN FC|date=10 January 2013|access-date=12 January 2013}}</ref> The following month, mere minutes after scoring the second goal at home against [[Rayo Vallecano]] and less than 20 minutes into the first half, he received two yellow cards within one minute in the eventual 2–0 home success, taking his red card tally with Real Madrid alone to 16; and 12 in the league.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/348295/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Real claim derby spoils|publisher=ESPN FC|date=17 February 2013|access-date=18 February 2013|archive-date=18 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318210419/https://web.archive.org/web/20140225192235/http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/348295/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/02/18/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1361187023.html|title=Sergio Ramos, en alerta roja|trans-title=Sergio Ramos, red alert|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=18 January 2013|access-date=18 February 2013|archive-date=4 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304231735/https://www.marca.com/2013/02/18/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1361187023.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In late February/early March 2013, due to the absence of [[Iker Casillas]] due to injury, Ramos [[Captain (association football)|captained]] Real to back-to-back wins over Barcelona in just four days: he netted the 2–1 home winner in the second game, heading home after a [[corner kick]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1360328/real-madrid-beats-barcelona-on-late-sergio-ramos-goal?cc=5739|title=Sergio Ramos heads Real past Barca|publisher=ESPN FC|date=2 March 2013|access-date=20 August 2013|archive-date=4 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504071844/http://www.espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1360328/real-madrid-beats-barcelona-on-late-sergio-ramos-goal?cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2013–14: Red card record and ''La Décima''====
On 14 December 2013, Ramos received a [[List of Real Madrid CF records and statistics|club record]] 18th red card for Real Madrid in a 2–2 draw at Osasuna,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1653387/real-madrid-appeal-sergio-ramos-record-18th-red-card?cc=3436|title=Madrid to appeal Ramos' 18th red card|publisher=ESPN FC|date=16 December 2013|access-date=16 December 2013|archive-date=1 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101072627/http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1653387/real-madrid-appeal-sergio-ramos-record-18th-red-card?cc=3436|url-status=live}}</ref> but the suspension was later lifted.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/97574-ramos-podra-jugar-valencia/|title=Sergio Ramos podrá jugar en Valencia|trans-title=Sergio Ramos will be able to play in Valencia|publisher=Defensa Central|language=es|date=18 December 2013|access-date=7 February 2014|archive-date=21 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621063348/https://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/97574-ramos-podra-jugar-valencia/|url-status=live}}</ref>

His 19th red card came in a 4–3 home defeat to Barcelona, on 23 March 2014.<ref name=retrospective/> On 26 April, Ramos scored a header against Osasuna in [[La Liga]] at the Bernabéu, in a counter-attack which he began with a strong tackle. It was his first goal in La Liga in six months, since his volley against Levante on match-day 8.<ref>{{cite news|title=4–0:Real Madrid feast on goals and carry o in the fighting for La Liga|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/04/4-0-real-madrid-feast-on-goals-and-carry-on-in-the-fight-for-la-liga|access-date=26 April 2014|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=26 April 2014|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727065439/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/04/4-0-real-madrid-feast-on-goals-and-carry-on-in-the-fight-for-la-liga|url-status=live}}</ref> On 29 April 2014, Ramos scored two headers in four minutes in a 4–0 away win against Bayern Munich in [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|the semi-finals of the Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c510b78cbc3-317cfe6f166f-1000--masterful-madrid-end-bayern-reign/|title=Masterful Madrid end Bayern reign|publisher=UEFA|date=29 April 2014|access-date=29 April 2014|archive-date=5 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005170632/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2014/matches/round=2000482/match=2011881/postmatch/report/index.html#masterful+madrid+bayern+reign|url-status=live}}</ref> with the tie ending with a 5–0 aggregate score and Madrid's qualification to the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] for the first time in twelve years. Ramos's brace against Bayern (4 minutes) was the fastest brace in [[UEFA Champions League]] semi-final history at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011881--bayern-munchen-vs-real-madrid/|title=Ancelotti delighted to end Madrid wait|publisher=UEFA|date=29 April 2014|access-date=29 April 2014|archive-date=24 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624161315/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2014/matches/round=2000482/match=2011881/postmatch/quotes/index.html?autoplay=true&vid=2089026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 May, Ramos scored in the 2–2 draw with Valencia at home in [[La Liga]] with another header, scoring in back-to-back league games.<ref>{{cite news|title=2–2:Real Madrid come from behind to earn a point in their bid to win La Liga|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/05/2-2-real-madrid-come-from-behind-to-earn-a-point-in-their-bid-to-win-la-liga|access-date=4 May 2014|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=4 May 2014|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727054302/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/05/2-2-real-madrid-come-from-behind-to-earn-a-point-in-their-bid-to-win-la-liga|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Ramos scored his first free-kick for a 1–1 draw away to Valladolid, having scored in three consecutive La Liga matches and scoring four consecutive matches for Real Madrid for the first time.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–1:Real Madrid slip up at Valladolid in their fight for the league title|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/05/1-1-real-madrid-slip-up-at-valladolid-in-their-fight-for-the-league-title|access-date=7 May 2014|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=7 May 2014|archive-date=18 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210618150759/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/05/1-1-real-madrid-slip-up-at-valladolid-in-their-fight-for-the-league-title|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 May, in the Champions League final against [[Atlético Madrid]], he headed home in the 93rd minute to tie the game 1–1, and Real Madrid went on to win 4–1 in [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]] to claim 'La Decima', their tenth trophy in the competition; he was also chosen by fans as [[Man of the match]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c51093bd4a7-41ccc377a75c-1000--madrid-finally-fulfil-decima-dream/|title=Madrid finally fulfil Décima dream|publisher=UEFA|date=24 May 2014|access-date=24 May 2014|archive-date=6 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706151008/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2014/matches/round=2000483/match=2011883/postmatch/report/index.html#madrid+finally+fulfil+decima+dream|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos ended [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14]] with 7 goals, which made it his highest scoring season for Real Madrid at the time.

====2014–20: Sustained success and captaincy====
Ramos started [[2014–15 Real Madrid CF season|2014–15 season]] on 12 August 2014 by playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–0 win against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] to win their first trophy of the season, the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]]. He then played the two-legged [[2014 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] final against [[Atlético Madrid]] with ''Los Blancos'' losing 2–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/11043806/Real-Madrid-vs-Atletico-Madrid-Spanish-Super-Cup-live.html|archive-url = https://archive.today/20140820084145/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/11043806/Real-Madrid-vs-Atletico-Madrid-Spanish-Super-Cup-live.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = 20 August 2014|title= Real Madrid 1 Atletico Madrid 1, Spanish Super Cup: as it happened|date=19 August 2014|work=The Daily Telegraph|access-date=20 August 2014}}</ref> Ramos scored his first goal of the season on 31 August in week two of [[2014–15 La Liga|La Liga]], a header in a 4–2 away loss against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/31/real-sociedad-real-madrid-la-liga-match-report|title=Real Sociedad's David Zurutuza scores twice to defeat Real Madrid|date=31 August 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=31 August 2014|archive-date=19 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319114148/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/31/real-sociedad-real-madrid-la-liga-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos scored his 50th Real Madrid goal which came off his knee on 8 November against Rayo Vallecano at the Bernabéu in La Liga as Real Madrid won 5–1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ramos scores 50th goal for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/11/ramos-scores-50th-goal-for-real-madrid|access-date=8 November 2014|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 November 2014|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727045719/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/11/ramos-scores-50th-goal-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref>

He scored in both the semi-final and [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final|the final]] of the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup]] and was voted the Player of the Match in both as Real Madrid won the tournament in Morocco. Ramos was also voted the player of the tournament, winning the Golden Ball.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ramos outshines the rest|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2014/m=12/news=ramos-outshines-the-rest-2495409-2495436.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221050123/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2014/m=12/news=ramos-outshines-the-rest-2495409-2495436.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 December 2014|access-date=21 December 2014|publisher=FIFA|date=20 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ramos, Golden Ball award at the Club World Cup|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/ramos-golden-ball-award-at-the-club-world-cup|access-date=20 December 2014|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=20 December 2014|archive-date=2 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802134847/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/ramos-golden-ball-award-at-the-club-world-cup|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Sergio Ramos desde el balcón de la Presidencia de la Comunidad de Madrid con la Úndecima Copa de Europa.jpg|thumb|180px|Ramos posing with the Champions League trophy at [[Puerta del Sol]], after the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|2015–16 season]]]]
Ramos agreed a new five-year contract with Real Madrid in August 2015, tying him to the club until 2020. He was also made captain after the transfer of Casillas to [[FC Porto|Porto]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Sergio Ramos signs his contract extension with Real Madrid|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/sergio-ramos-signs-his-contract-extension-with-real-madrid|access-date=17 August 2015|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 August 2015|archive-date=24 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724072518/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/sergio-ramos-signs-his-contract-extension-with-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 November, Ramos scored his first goal of the season away to Sevilla. In scoring with an overhead kick he was forced to be substituted due to landing on his injured left shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=3–2: Real Madrid slip up in the Sánchez Pizjuán|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/11/3-2-real-madrid-slip-up-in-the-sanchez-pizjuan|access-date=4 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=29 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729035747/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/11/3-2-real-madrid-slip-up-in-the-sanchez-pizjuan|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 December 2015, Ramos captained Madrid to a 10–2 victory over [[Rayo Vallecano]], the club's highest scoring La Liga victory in 55 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35141793|title=Real Madrid 10–2 Rayo Vallecano|date=20 December 2015|publisher=BBC|access-date=13 February 2018|archive-date=26 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426172904/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35141793|url-status=live}}</ref> The following 13 March, he received his 20th red card for Real Madrid in a 2–1 win over [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], having earlier scored the game's opening goal with a header from an [[Isco]] corner kick. On 2 April 2016, he returned from suspension in a 2–1 victory against Barcelona at the [[Camp Nou]], where he was again sent off, receiving his 21st red card and fourth in a [[El Clásico|Clásico]] fixture.<ref name=retrospective/>

Real Madrid reached the [[2016 UEFA Champions League Final]], where they faced [[Atlético Madrid]]. Ramos once again scored in a final, putting Real ahead in the first half. At the time, he was just the fifth player to score in two different Champions League Finals after [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], [[Samuel Eto'o]], Lionel Messi and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]. After a second-half equalizer from Atlético, he then scored a penalty in the shoot-out which resulted in Real Madrid winning 5–3; thus, he lifted his first UEFA Champions League trophy as a captain.<ref name="2015–16 CL">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|date=28 May 2016|publisher=UEFA|access-date=29 May 2016|archive-date=10 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110225552/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2016/matches/round=2000638/match=2015789/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> According to author [[Michael Cox (journalist)|Michael Cox]], he also notably "tipped the balance of the game toward Real Madrid" by tripping [[Yannick Carrasco]] up and stopping a three-on-one counter in stoppage time, with 30 seconds remaining and the score 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-premier-league/23/blog/post/3710171/footballs-dark-arts-your-guide-to-the-set-piece-trickery-diving-and-sneaky-fouls-that-make-a-difference|title=Football's dark arts: Your guide to the set-piece trickery, diving and sneaky fouls that make a difference|publisher=[[ESPN]]|last=Cox|first=Michael|author-link=Michael Cox (journalist)|date=29 November 2018|access-date=27 July 2019|archive-date=28 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128203013/https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-premier-league/23/blog/post/3710171/footballs-dark-arts-your-guide-to-the-set-piece-trickery-diving-and-sneaky-fouls-that-make-a-difference|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named [[man of the match]] by [[UEFA]] after the game.<ref name="2015–16 CL"/> By winning the final, Real Madrid earned the right to play against the winners of the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], in the [[2016 UEFA Super Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c5112185f92-bb13acef9423-1000--real-madrid-play-sevilla-in-uefa-super-cup/|title=Real Madrid play Sevilla in UEFA Super Cup|publisher=UEFA|date=28 May 2016|access-date=27 July 2019|archive-date=14 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180914125939/https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/newsid=2363901.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos ended the [[2015–16 Real Madrid CF season|2015–16 season]] with three goals in 33 games which was his lowest goal tally and the fewest matches he played in any season at Real Madrid till then, due to ongoing injuries.

[[File:Felicidades al Real Madrid, campeón de liga (34824732435).jpg|thumb|left|230px|upright|Ramos and Community of Madrid President [[Cristina Cifuentes]] with the [[2016–17 La Liga]] trophy during celebrations in Madrid.]]
Ramos started in the [[2016 UEFA Super Cup]] in [[Trondheim]], scoring Real Madrid's equalizing second goal of the match in the 93rd minute, and hence bringing the game into extra-time. Real Madrid were the eventual 3–2 winners, with Ramos being named [[man of the match]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Carvajal wonder goal wins Super Cup for Madrid|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/match/2019261--real-madrid-vs-sevilla/|publisher=UEFA|access-date=10 August 2016|archive-date=29 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629230447/http://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/season=2016/matches/round=2000778/match=2019261/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 3 December 2016, he scored his fourth Clásico goal, an equalizer against Barcelona in a 1–1 draw at the [[Camp Nou]] in the 90th minute, extending Madrid's unbeaten run to 33 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ramos keeps Real Madrid unbeaten as Barcelona suffer late in El Clasico|url=http://www.espnfc.com/blog/the-match/60/post/3009094/ramos-keeps-real-madrid-unbeaten-as-barcelona-suffer-late-in-el-clasico|website=ESPN FC|access-date=3 December 2016|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615135846/http://www.espnfc.com/blog/the-match/60/post/3009094/ramos-keeps-real-madrid-unbeaten-as-barcelona-suffer-late-in-el-clasico|url-status=live}}</ref> One week later, he scored another late goal, this time in the 92nd minute, to help Madrid claim a 3–2 victory against Deportivo La Coruña.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Deportivo de La Coruña|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38203086|access-date=10 December 2016|archive-date=31 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831091313/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38203086|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 15 January 2017, Ramos scored an own goal late in the game against Sevilla which levelled the scores at 1–1. Eventually Real Madrid lost the match 2–1 in stoppage time, thus ending their unbeaten streak at 40 matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/755/europe/2017/01/15/31575912/ramos-turns-liga-race-on-its-head-as-madrid-lose-control-and |title=Ramos turns Liga race on its head as Madrid lose control and unbeaten record|date=15 January 2017}}</ref> A week later, he scored both goals in a 2–1 win over [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], registering his 50th goal in La Liga.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2017/01/21/primera/1485018162_436926.html|title=Sergio Ramos ya ha marcado más que Bale en esta temporada|date=21 January 2017|work=AS|language=es|access-date=21 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202202657/http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2017/01/21/primera/1485018162_436926.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 February, in a 3–1 victory against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], Ramos played his 500th match with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/02/sergio-ramos-has-played-500-games-for-real-madrid|title=Sergio Ramos has played 500 games for Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=11 February 2017|access-date=12 February 2017|archive-date=24 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724072521/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/02/sergio-ramos-has-played-500-games-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Round-of-16|UEFA Champions League round of 16]] second leg, Ramos scored an important equalizing header against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] in a 3–1 away win as Real Madrid qualified to the quarter-final after winning 6–2 on aggregate. On 12 March, Ramos scored another late header winner for Real Madrid, this time against [[Real Betis]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] in a 2–1 win, taking his goal tally to 10 for the season – scoring double digit goals in a season for the first time in his career. Ramos's winner put Real Madrid back at the top of the [[2016–17 La Liga|La Liga]] table.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/03/2-1-sergio-ramos-fires-madrid-back-to-the-top|title=Real Madrid-Betis: 2–1: Sergio Ramos fires Madrid back to the top|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=8 December 2018|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061039/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/03/2-1-sergio-ramos-fires-madrid-back-to-the-top|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 April 2017, Ramos was sent off for the 22nd time in his Real Madrid career and fifth time in an El Clásico, after a straight red card for a two-footed challenge on Lionel Messi during a Barcelona counter-attack in their 3–2 home defeat.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.in/football/report?gameId=458756|title=Messi brace pulls Barcelona even in La Liga after thrilling Clasico win|publisher=ESPN|date=24 April 2017|access-date=31 March 2021|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062543/https://www.espn.in/football/report?gameId=458756|url-status=live}}</ref> Real Madrid won their 33rd [[2016–17 La Liga|La Liga]] title, giving Ramos his fourth league title overall and first as captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|date=21 May 2017|work=laliga.es|access-date=22 May 2017|archive-date=12 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712180825/http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga|date=21 May 2017|publisher=BBC|access-date=13 February 2018|archive-date=26 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226192537/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|url-status=live}}</ref> They went on to win their first league and European Cup double since 1957–58 season, as the team defeated [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final]]. This also made Ramos the first player to captain a team to back-to-back European Cups in the [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League history#1993 – The birth of the Champions League and Marseille attain first title|UEFA Champions League era]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|date=3 June 2017|publisher=UEFA|access-date=4 June 2017|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331042605/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2017/matches/round=2000787/match=2019641/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> His ten goals in [[2016–17 Real Madrid CF season|2016–17]] made it his then-highest scoring season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2017/05/29/player-guide-for-champions-league-holder-real-madrid/102286288/|title=Player guide for Champions League holder Real Madrid|date=29 May 2017|work=USA Today|access-date=5 June 2017|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330205326/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2017/05/29/player-guide-for-champions-league-holder-real-madrid/102286288/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Real Madrid C.F. the Winner Of The Champions League in 2018 (1).jpg|thumb|right|247px|Ramos hoisting the [[European Champion Clubs' Cup]] as Real Madrid celebrate winning the UEFA Champions League, on [[2018 UEFA Champions League Final|26 May 2018]]]]
[[File:Recepción Real Madrid en la Comunidad de Madrid (40650243260).jpg|thumb|right|247px|Ramos kissing the Champions League trophy during the [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|2018 title]] celebrations in Madrid.]]
On 20 August 2017, in Real Madrid's first game of the [[2017–18 La Liga]], he received his 23rd career red card. It was his 18th in La Liga, a joint highest record.<!--rem deprecated source (dailymail)--> He went on to break that record, seeing his 19th La Liga red in a 0–0 draw with [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-sets-dubious-la-liga-record/1pu01uascged61r2ddgfcif45p|title=Real Madrid News: Sergio Ramos sets La Liga red card record {{!}} Goal.com|access-date=3 December 2017|archive-date=19 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719222926/https://www.goal.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-sets-dubious-la-liga-record/1pu01uascged61r2ddgfcif45p|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos scored his first goal of the season on 13 September in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], scoring a bicycle kick against [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] on match-day 1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/3-0-real-madrid-make-light-work-of-apoel-as-ronaldo-nets-a-brace|title=3–0: Real Madrid make light work of APOEL as Ronaldo nebrace|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=8 December 2018|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330181806/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/3-0-real-madrid-make-light-work-of-apoel-as-ronaldo-nets-a-brace|url-status=live}}</ref> In [[2017–18 La Liga|La Liga]], Ramos scored four goals, including two penalties – against Leganes and Sevilla. During the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], he made eleven appearances, while scoring one goal, when Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall Champions League title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|date=26 May 2018|publisher=UEFA|access-date=27 May 2018|archive-date=27 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527203029/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2018/matches/round=2000885/match=2021711/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos's performance in [[2018 UEFA Champions League Final|the final]], however, was met with criticism;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/05/sergio-ramos-salah-karius-champions-league-real-madrid|title=Real Madrid's Sergio Ramos hits back over Salah and Karius criticism|date=5 June 2018|work=The Guardian|access-date=20 June 2018|archive-date=16 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316053935/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/05/sergio-ramos-salah-karius-champions-league-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> a challenge on [[Mohamed Salah]] resulted in the Egyptian dislocating his shoulder and missing the rest of the game,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44258022|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Liverpool|date=26 May 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=20 June 2018|archive-date=21 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190521142709/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44258022|url-status=live}}</ref> and he hit Liverpool keeper [[Loris Karius]] in the head with his elbow, the goalkeeper later being diagnosed with concussion.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reaction: The moment 'dirty thug' Sergio Ramos cruelled Salah's UCL hopes |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/uefa-champions-league/reaction-the-moment-dirty-thug-sergio-ramos-cruelled-salahs-ucl-hopes/news-story/7a22ab3c7e2087edf6bf062978259c75 |date=26 May 2018 |access-date=15 June 2018 |archive-date=31 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331020147/https://www.foxsports.com.au/football/uefa-champions-league/reaction-the-moment-dirty-thug-sergio-ramos-cruelled-salahs-ucl-hopes/news-story/7a22ab3c7e2087edf6bf062978259c75?nk=c88f65a86383d9dd645a148cfa4f46b6-1553984106 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44363648|title=Loris Karius: Liverpool keeper concussed during Champions League final – doctors|date=4 June 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=20 June 2018|archive-date=4 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180604191659/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44363648|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos later denied that he intentionally hit Karius, saying that [[Virgil van Dijk]] pushed him into Karius.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thescore.com/chlg/news/1554166|title=Real's Ramos: Role in Liverpool injuries 'blown out of all proportion'|work=theScore.com|access-date=25 October 2018|archive-date=20 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230220044332/https://www.thescore.com/chlg/news/1554166|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos became the first player to captain a team to three consecutive Champions League triumphs, having now lifted the Champions League in every season as captain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/sergio-ramos-first-player-in-42-years-to-lead-his-side-to-3-ucl-titles-1242909-2018-05-27|title=Sergio Ramos first player in 42 years to lead his side to 3 UCL titles|author=Ranit Das|date=27 May 2018|website=India Today|access-date=20 January 2021|archive-date=18 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218084911/https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/sergio-ramos-first-player-in-42-years-to-lead-his-side-to-3-ucl-titles-1242909-2018-05-27|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ramos began the [[2018–19 Real Madrid CF season|2018–19]] season scoring a penalty in an eventual 4–2 loss to Atlético Madrid in the [[2018 UEFA Super Cup]]. Taking the penalty ensured Ramos would be the team's new penalty taker with the departure of [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribuna.com/en/realmadrid/news/2858685/|title=Sergio Ramos steps up as the new Real Madrid penalty taker|work=[[tribuna.com]]|access-date=16 August 2018|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330181816/https://tribuna.com/en/realmadrid/news/2858685/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 26 August 2018, Ramos scored another penalty in Real Madrid's 4–1 away win against [[Girona FC|Girona]],<ref>{{cite news |author=Dunne, Robbie |title=Real Madrid's Sergio Ramos: Giving Karim Benzema penalty builds 'spirit' |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37560722/giving-karim-benzema-penalty-builds-spirit |work=ESPN |publisher=ESPN Enterprises, LLC |date=28 August 2018 |access-date=4 October 2026}}</ref> making him the only player along with [[Lionel Messi]] to score in each of the last 15 [[La Liga]] seasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Los dos únicos jugadores que han anotado en LaLiga durante 15 temporadas consecutivas |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/09/07/los-dos-unicos-jugadores-que-han-anotado-en-laliga-durante-15-temporadas-consecutivas |work=Sports Illustrated |publisher=Minute Media |language=es |date=7 September 2018 |access-date=4 October 2026}}</ref> One week later, Ramos scored his third penalty of the season, against Leganes in a 4–1 win at the Santiago Bernabéu – his first goal at home since March 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/4-1-real-madrid-run-riot-to-stay-top|title=4–1: Real Madrid amongst the goals and 100% start to the LaLiga season|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=1 September 2018|archive-date=29 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729132225/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/09/4-1-real-madrid-run-riot-to-stay-top|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 25 December 2018, Ramos played his 400th La Liga match for Real Madrid in a 2–1 loss at home to Levante, becoming only the tenth Real Madrid player to reach this milestone.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/ramos-and-casemiro-make-400th-and-100th-laliga-appearances-respectively|title=Ramos and Casemiro make 400th and 100th LaLiga appearances respectively|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=20 October 2018|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718104221/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/10/ramos-and-casemiro-make-400th-and-100th-laliga-appearances-respectively|url-status=live}}</ref> After a run of poor results and the sacking of [[Julen Lopetegui]], Ramos scored his first goal for Real Madrid in two months through a [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka]], against Real Valladolid in [[Santiago Solari]]'s first [[2018–19 La Liga]] game in charge of ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/2-0-a-hard-earned-win-at-the-bernabeu|title=2–0: A hard-earned win at the Bernabéu|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=3 November 2018|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727070008/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/2-0-a-hard-earned-win-at-the-bernabeu|url-status=live}}</ref> Two weeks later, on 11 November, Ramos scored another Panenka against Celta Vigo – making them the 25th different team he scored against in La Liga.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/11/11/football/1541964045_130625.html?omnaut=1|title=Celta Vigo 2–4 Real Madrid: Solari makes it four wins in four|work=en.as.com|access-date=11 November 2018|archive-date=15 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115030920/https://en.as.com/en/2018/11/11/football/1541964045_130625.html?omnaut=1|url-status=dead}}</ref> This was Ramos's third Panenka from his last four penalties, with the inventor of the penalty, [[Antonín Panenka]], saying Ramos was the best 'imitator' of his penalty technique.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/11/13/football/1542105571_893059.html|title=Panenka proud Sergio Ramos imitates his penalties|work=as.com|access-date=13 November 2018|archive-date=13 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190713075837/https://en.as.com/en/2018/11/13/football/1542105571_893059.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> With five goals in the first three months of the season, Ramos had his best goal-scoring start to a season at Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/ramos-enjoying-most-prolific-start-to-campaign-in-madrid-career|title=Ramos enjoying most prolific start to campaign in Madrid career|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=16 November 2018|archive-date=24 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190424092323/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/11/ramos-enjoying-most-prolific-start-to-campaign-in-madrid-career|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup]], Ramos played in both Real Madrid's semi-final against [[Kashima Antlers]] and the final against [[Al Ain FC|Al Ain]]. Ramos scored a header in [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup Final|the final]] as Real Madrid won 3–1 to claim their third consecutive FIFA Club World Cup.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-make-history-in-unexpected-final|title=FIFA Club World Cup UAE 2018 – Real Madrid make history in unexpected final|website=FIFA|access-date=24 December 2018|archive-date=14 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200414144402/https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-make-history-in-unexpected-final|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos became the first player to lift three consecutive [[FIFA Club World Cup]]s while also becoming the first defender to score in two Club World Cup Finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/4-1-a-seventh-club-world-cup-title|title=Real Madrid-Al Ain: 4–1: A seventh Club World Cup title|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=24 December 2018|archive-date=11 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711204541/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/12/4-1-a-seventh-club-world-cup-title|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 9 January 2019, Ramos scored a penalty in the [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] game against [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], which was his 100th career goal, excluding two goals for Sevilla's [[Sevilla Atlético|reserve team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/3-0-real-madrid-pick-up-a-convincing-win-to-move-closer-to-copa-del-rey-quarter-finals|title=Real Madrid-Leganés: 3–0: El Real Madrid golea y se acerca a cuartos de la Copa|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=11 January 2019|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062553/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/3-0-real-madrid-pick-up-a-convincing-win-to-move-closer-to-copa-del-rey-quarter-finals|url-status=live}}</ref> To celebrate the goal, Ramos chose to show the number 100 with his fingers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/sergio-ramos-scores-his-100th-professional-goal|title=Sergio Ramos scores his 100th professional goal|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=11 January 2019|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727141225/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/sergio-ramos-scores-his-100th-professional-goal|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 January, Ramos scored a brace against Girona in the [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey quarter-final first leg]] in a 4–2 home win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/4-2-real-madrid-move-a-step-closer-to-the-semi-finals|title=Real Madrid-Girona: 4–2: Real Madrid move a step closer to the semi-finals|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=28 January 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330183312/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/4-2-real-madrid-move-a-step-closer-to-the-semi-finals|url-status=live}}</ref> It was Ramos's fourth brace for Real Madrid and his first in the Copa del Rey.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/ramos-real-madrid-doubles|title=Ramos Real Madrid doubles|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=28 January 2019|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718094150/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/ramos-real-madrid-doubles|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Ramos scored his tenth goal of the campaign with a header against Espanyol in a 4–2 away win, which was also his 60th [[La Liga]] goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/2-4-benzema-brace-sets-up-big-win-for-the-whites|title=2–4: Benzema brace sets up big win for the Whites|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=28 January 2019|archive-date=5 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405140715/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/2-4-benzema-brace-sets-up-big-win-for-the-whites|url-status=live}}</ref> With ten goals to his name, Ramos equalled his highest-scoring season at Real Madrid which he set in [[2016–17 Real Madrid CF season|2016–17]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/ramos-equals-his-highest-scoring-season-at-real-madrid|title=Ramos equals his highest-scoring season at Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=28 January 2019|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062552/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/ramos-equals-his-highest-scoring-season-at-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 February 2019, Sergio Ramos was playing in [[El Clásico|the Clásico]] for the 40th time. Three days later, in the [[Madrid Derby]] against Atlético Madrid, Ramos scored his eighth penalty of the season and his 11th goal in all competitions – making it his best goal-scoring season at Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-beats-his-record-for-goals-scored-in-one-season|title=Sergio Ramos beats his record for goals scored in one season|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=11 February 2019|archive-date=17 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117071743/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-beats-his-record-for-goals-scored-in-one-season|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, in the 2–1 [[2018-19 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Round-of-16|Champions League Round of 16]] first leg [[Johan Cruyff Arena|away]] win over [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], Ramos became just the seventh player to play 600 matches for Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-600-games-for-real-madrid|title=Sergio Ramos, 600 games for Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2019|archive-date=19 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191219065944/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-600-games-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> In the match against Ajax, Ramos was booked for what seemed to be a needless challenge in the 90th minute. The booking meant that Ramos would miss the second leg against Ajax at the Santiago Bernabéu due a suspension of accumulating yellow cards. This sparked controversy after Ramos hinted to journalists in a post match interview that the yellow card was deliberate, which violates [[UEFA]]'s rules.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/02/13/5c649f90e2704e965e8b45c8.html|title=Ramos on his yellow card: I'd be lying if I said I didn't force it|date=13 February 2019|website=MARCA in English|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=14 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214060422/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/02/13/5c649f90e2704e965e8b45c8.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Two and a half weeks later, UEFA opened a disciplinary investigation regarding this matter and decided to give Ramos a two-game ban, meaning he will also miss both the Champions League Round of 16-second leg against Ajax and the quarter-final first leg were Real Madrid to qualify.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/11651208/real-madrid-captain-sergio-ramos-banned-for-two-european-matches-for-deliberate-booking|title=Real Madrid captain Sergio Ramos banned for two European matches for 'deliberate booking'|website=Sky Sports|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=5 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605083940/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/11651208/real-madrid-captain-sergio-ramos-banned-for-two-european-matches-for-deliberate-booking|url-status=live}}</ref> Due to Real Madrid's elimination by Ajax, the suspension carried onto the next season and Ramos missed the first Champions League game of the 2019–20 season against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37576590/marcelo-madrid-7-players-psg|title=Marcelo out, Madrid without 7 players for PSG|date=16 September 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=17 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417042910/https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/3944172/marcelo-outmadrid-without-7-players-for-psg|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 17 February, Ramos played his 601st match for Real Madrid, against Girona in La Liga, equalling the record of Real Madrid legends [[Fernando Hierro]] and [[Paco Gento]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-moves-level-with-gento-and-hierro-in-appearances|title=Sergio Ramos moves level with Gento and Hierro in appearances|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=21 February 2019|archive-date=21 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221115136/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-moves-level-with-gento-and-hierro-in-appearances|url-status=live}}</ref> Ten days later, Ramos played in his 41st El Clásico, in the Copa del Rey semi-final second leg at home. This was Ramos's 602nd match for Real Madrid, taking up to him fifth in Real Madrid's all-time appearances list.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-has-now-played-the-fifth-most-games-in-the-history-of-real-madrid|title=Sergio Ramos has now played the fifth most games in the history of Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330044648/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/02/sergio-ramos-has-now-played-the-fifth-most-games-in-the-history-of-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 March, Ramos played in the La Liga El Clásico at the Bernabéu, making him equal the all-time record of Paco Gento, [[Manolo Sanchís]] and [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] by playing in 42 Clasicos.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/futbol/20190303/sergio-ramos-alcanza-clasicos-gento-xavi-sanchis/380212566_0.html|title=Sergio Ramos alcanza los 42 Clásicos: iguala a Gento, Xavi y Sanchís|date=3 March 2019|website=El Español|language=es-ES|access-date=30 March 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330045143/https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/futbol/20190303/sergio-ramos-alcanza-clasicos-gento-xavi-sanchis/380212566_0.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 March, Real Madrid were eliminated from the Champions League by Ajax after being thrashed 4–1 at the Santiago Bernabéu (aggregate 5–3 for Ajax).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11945/11655986/real-madrid-1-4-ajax-3-5-on-agg-ajax-stun-holders-at-bernabeu|title=Real Madrid 1–4 Ajax (3–5 on agg): Ajax stun holders at Bernabeu|website=Sky Sports|access-date=30 March 2019|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061040/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11945/11655986/real-madrid-1-4-ajax-3-5-on-agg-ajax-stun-holders-at-bernabeu|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos did not feature due to being suspended after forcing a yellow card in the first leg, thus facing criticism for doing so.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2019/03/sergio-ramos-ajax|title=Sergio Ramos' intentional suspension backfires for Real Madrid vs. Ajax|date=5 March 2019|website=For The Win|access-date=30 March 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330044840/https://ftw.usatoday.com/2019/03/sergio-ramos-ajax|url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, Ramos faced even more criticism as he was caught with a camera crew in the stands, filming for his new [[Amazon Prime]] documentary.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2019/03/05/sergio-ramos-real-madrid-champions-league-loss-ajax|title=Sergio Ramos filming Amazon doc during Ajax loss|magazine=Sports Illustrated|access-date=30 March 2019|archive-date=19 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191119124928/https://www.si.com/soccer/2019/03/05/sergio-ramos-real-madrid-champions-league-loss-ajax|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos took to his [[Twitter]] and [[Instagram]] accounts to discuss the controversy surrounding his actions, in which he admitted forcing the yellow card against Ajax in the first leg "was an error and I take the blame 200%". Regarding filming the documentary, Ramos claimed there were "certain commitments" made prior and he did not imagine the game would pan out as it did.<ref name="marca.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/03/11/5c8651eee2704e03838b4568.html|title=Sergio Ramos addresses key points of Real Madrid crisis in self-interview|date=11 March 2019|website=MARCA in English|access-date=30 March 2019|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330044754/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/03/11/5c8651eee2704e03838b4568.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos picked up a calf injury at the start of April, which saw him miss the rest of the campaign and the final eight La Liga matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/04/12/football/1555080469_394950.html|title=Sergio Ramos out with calf injury|date=12 April 2019|website=AS.com|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=26 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126194916/https://en.as.com/en/2019/04/12/football/1555080469_394950.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:FC RB Salzburg versus Real Madrid (Testspiel, 7. August 2019) 09.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Ramos playing for Real Madrid in 2019]]
Ramos's first goal of the season was a header in his first [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match of the campaign, against [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] on 1 October at home. The goal came at a vital time as Real Madrid were 2–0 down by half-time but were able to make a comeback after another header by [[Casemiro]]. This was also Ramos's first Champions League goal in two seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/2-2-real-madrid-claim-draw-against-brugge|title=Real Madrid-Club Brugge: 2–2: Real Madrid claim draw against Brugge|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=24 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624001555/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/10/2-2-real-madrid-claim-draw-against-brugge|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 October, Ramos scored from the penalty-spot in a 5–0 home victory over [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], continuing his run of scoring in 16 straight La Liga seasons, again equalling Messi.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/10/30/5dba036022601d044b8b45d4.html|title=Sergio Ramos continues his run of scoring in 16 straight seasons|website=Marca|location=Spain|date=30 October 2019|access-date=2 November 2019|archive-date=8 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191108171533/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/10/30/5dba036022601d044b8b45d4.html|url-status=live}}</ref> One week later, on 6 November, Ramos scored his first penalty in the Champions League, which came against [[Galatasaray S.K.|Galatasaray]] in a 6–0 home win. It was another 'Panenka' style penalty and also meant that Ramos scored in two Champions League group matches in the same season for the first time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/06/6-0-rodrygo-hat-trick-brings-the-whites-closer-to-the-last-16|title=Real Madrid-Galatasaray: 6–0: Rodrygo 'Hat-trick' brings the Whites closer to the last-16|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727062840/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/11/06/6-0-rodrygo-hat-trick-brings-the-whites-closer-to-the-last-16|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 December, Ramos played in his 43rd El Clasico, claiming the all-time appearance record for this historic fixture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/17/sergio-ramos-claims-all-time-clasico-appearance-record|title=Sergio Ramos claims all-time Clásico appearance record|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061044/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/12/17/sergio-ramos-claims-all-time-clasico-appearance-record|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 January 2020, Ramos scored the winning penalty in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shoot-out]] against Atletico Madrid in the [[2020 Supercopa de España Final|Supercopa de España final]] in [[Jeddah]] as Real Madrid won 4–1 on penalties after a 0–0 draw after [[Overtime (association football)|extra time]]. This was the first time in Ramos's career that he scored a winning penalty in a shoot-out.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/12/0-0-eleventh-spanish-super-cup|title=Real Madrid-Atlético: 0–0: Eleventh Spanish Super Cup!|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=1 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801115243/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/12/0-0-eleventh-spanish-super-cup|url-status=live}}</ref> The 2020 Supercopa title was Ramos's 21st trophy with Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/13/ramos-and-marcelos-21-titles-with-real-madrid|title=Ramos and Marcelos 21 titles with Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=8 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200408035914/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/01/13/ramos-and-marcelos-21-titles-with-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> A month later, Ramos scored another header in La Liga, this time away to [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] as Real Madrid won 4–1 to maintain top position in the table.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/09/1-4-the-leaders-come-from-behind-at-el-sadar|title=Osasuna-Real Madrid: 1–4: The leaders come from behind at El Sadar|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727053417/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/02/09/1-4-the-leaders-come-from-behind-at-el-sadar|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos's goal at [[El Sadar Stadium|El Sadar]] meant that he had scored in 20 different La Liga stadiums.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/02/10/5e40a4a746163fa5588b4568.html|title=Sergio Ramos puts in another pin: He's scored at 20 different stadiums|date=10 February 2020|website=MARCA in English|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=17 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200317135307/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/02/10/5e40a4a746163fa5588b4568.html|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's first La Liga goal of 2020, meaning he was the only player to score in La Liga in each of the last 17 calendar years – dating back to 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2874445-lionel-messi-sergio-ramos-and-la-liga-team-of-the-week-after-matchday-22|title=Lionel Messi, Sergio Ramos and La Liga Team of the Week After Matchday 22|last=Verschueren|first=Gianni|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=14 February 2020|archive-date=4 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204175104/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2874445-lionel-messi-sergio-ramos-and-la-liga-team-of-the-week-after-matchday-22|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 26 February 2020, Ramos equalled the record of red cards received in the UEFA Champions League. With four red cards, he shares the unwanted record with [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] and [[Edgar Davids]].<ref name="goal.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/ramos-equals-champions-league-red-card-record/f8u5uw9bssx21403lbzi2rzus|title=Ramos equals Champions League red card record with Man City dismissal {{!}} Goal.com|website=Goal.com|access-date=27 February 2020|archive-date=27 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227161110/https://www.goal.com/en/news/ramos-equals-champions-league-red-card-record/f8u5uw9bssx21403lbzi2rzus|url-status=live}}</ref> This dismissal came in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the Round of 16 first leg, for a [[Professional foul|tactical foul]] on City striker [[Gabriel Jesus]].<ref name="goal.com"/> Four days later, Ramos featured in Real Madrid's 2–0 win over Barcelona at home in La Liga to leapfrog them into first place.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Madrid-Barcelona: 2–0: Clásico win and top spot for Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/01/2-0-clasico-win-and-top-spot-for-madrid|access-date=29 June 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727064528/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/01/2-0-clasico-win-and-top-spot-for-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's 21st consecutive Clasico in all competitions and his 30th in La Liga with Real Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sergio Ramos has played in the last 20 Clásicos|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/01/sergio-ramos-has-played-in-the-last-20-clasicos|access-date=29 June 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727065835/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/03/01/sergio-ramos-has-played-in-the-last-20-clasicos|url-status=live}}</ref>

When La Liga restarted after a three-month hiatus due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]], Ramos scored in Real Madrid's first game back against [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] on 14 June at the [[Alfredo di Stéfano Stadium]] in a 3–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Madrid – Éibar {{!}} La Liga Matchday 28|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/football/games/la-liga/real-madrid-eibar---2020-03-15|access-date=29 June 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727044234/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/football/games/la-liga/real-madrid-eibar---2020-03-15|url-status=live}}</ref> He also scored the first goal at this stadium in its inaugural match in May 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|date=8 June 2020|title=Ramos, man who got the first goal at Di Stéfano stadium|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/ramos-man-who-got-the-first-goal-at-di-stefano-stadium-844400|access-date=29 June 2020|website=BeSoccer|archive-date=29 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629152121/https://www.besoccer.com/new/ramos-man-who-got-the-first-goal-at-di-stefano-stadium-844400|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos's goal began with him winning the ball back from Eibar's attack a few meters outside Madrid's own penalty area and ran 70 meters across the pitch to find the pass from [[Eden Hazard]] to score his first La Liga goal from open play in over five years.<ref>{{Cite web|date=14 June 2020|title=Ramos sprints 70 metres to score Real Madrid's second goal|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/06/14/5ee6704d22601dbb0e8b45a3.html|access-date=29 June 2020|website=MARCA in English|archive-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630015356/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/06/14/5ee6704d22601dbb0e8b45a3.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 June, Ramos scored a penalty for Real Madrid in their 2–1 win against Real Sociedad at the [[Anoeta Stadium|Anoeta]], which was the 20th consecutive penalty he converted for club and country (including shoot-outs).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Sociedad-Real Madrid: 1–2: Madrid win and move top of LaLiga|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/21/1-2-madrid-win-and-move-top-of-laliga|access-date=1 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727065959/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/21/1-2-madrid-win-and-move-top-of-laliga|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Ramos scored a free-kick against in a 2–0 win over Mallorca at the Alfredo di Stefano to become La Liga's all-time highest scoring defender with 68 goals, surpassing [[Ronald Koeman]]'s 67 with Barcelona.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Madrid star Ramos becomes top-scoring defender in La Liga history {{!}} Goal.com|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/real-madrid-star-sergio-ramos-becomes-la-ligas-top-scoring/ex2o0e4laovz14woa5v4soeqx|access-date=1 July 2020|website=goal.com|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061040/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/real-madrid-star-sergio-ramos-becomes-la-ligas-top-scoring/ex2o0e4laovz14woa5v4soeqx|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos's free-kick was also his eighth La Liga goal of the season, making it his most prolific league campaign to date and his tenth in all competitions – hitting double figures for a third season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sergio Ramos enjoying his highest-scoring LaLiga campaign|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/26/sergio-ramos-enjoying-his-highest-scoring-laliga-campaign|access-date=1 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=1 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701191143/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/26/sergio-ramos-enjoying-his-highest-scoring-laliga-campaign|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 June, Ramos featured in the 1–0 away league win against Espanyol, heading the ball down right outside the Espanyol penalty area to [[Karim Benzema]] who eventually assisted Casemiro to score the winner right before half-time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Espanyol-Real Madrid: 0–1: Real Madrid extend their lead a[sic] the top|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/28/0-1-real-madrid-extend-their-lead-a-the-top|access-date=1 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727060518/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/28/0-1-real-madrid-extend-their-lead-a-the-top|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's 645th match for Madrid, moving him up to fourth in the club's all-time most appearances list joint with [[Santillana (footballer)|Santillana]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos moves into fourth place on the all-time madridista appearances list|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/28/ramos-moves-into-fourth-place-on-the-all-time-madridista-appearances-list|access-date=1 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727060432/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/06/28/ramos-moves-into-fourth-place-on-the-all-time-madridista-appearances-list|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 2 July 2020, Ramos scored his fifteenth consecutive penalty for Real Madrid in the 79th minute which proved to be the winner in a 1–0 home win against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] – opening up a four-point
