advantage at the top of La Liga.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Madrid-Getafe: 1–0: The LaLiga leaders win again to open up a 4-point advantage|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/02/1-0-the-laliga-leaders-win-again-to-open-up-a-4-point-advantage|access-date=4 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727050838/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/02/1-0-the-laliga-leaders-win-again-to-open-up-a-4-point-advantage|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos 15 penalties without missing|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/fans/videos/2020/07/ramos-15-penalties-without-missing|access-date=4 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727063913/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/fans/videos/2020/07/ramos-15-penalties-without-missing|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's ninth league goal of the season – equaling the record set by [[Argentina national football team|Argentine international]] defender [[Ezequiel Garay]] in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006-07]] while playing for [[Real Racing Club de Santander|Racing Santander]] for a defender with the most goals in a single La Liga season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=25 June 2020|title=Real Madrid : Sergio Ramos s'offre un record historique|url=https://www.onzemondial.com/liga/2019-2020/real-madrid-sergio-ramos-s-offre-un-record-historique-222088|access-date=4 July 2020|website=Onze Mondial|language=fr|archive-date=4 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200704081944/https://www.onzemondial.com/liga/2019-2020/real-madrid-sergio-ramos-s-offre-un-record-historique-222088|url-status=live}}</ref> The penalty against Getafe meant that Ramos had equalled his best goal scoring season (11 goals) which was set the previous season. Ramos had now scored in four out of six of Madrid's matches since the restart, more than any other player.<ref>{{Cite web|date=3 July 2020|title=Ramos: The unexpected 'Pichichi'|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/03/5eff6460268e3ebf6c8b45a3.html|access-date=4 July 2020|website=MARCA in English|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061042/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/03/5eff6460268e3ebf6c8b45a3.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, the goal was his 100th career club goal, and his 70th in La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2020-07-03-another-match-another-record-sergio-ramos-marks-his-450th-la-liga-appearance-for-real-mad/ |title=Another match, another record: Sergio Ramos marks his 450th La Liga appearance for Real Madrid with winner over Getafe |publisher=[[Tribuna.com]]|last1=Shchepanskyi |first1=Den |date=3 July 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020 |archive-date=5 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200705185114/https://tribuna.com/en/realmadrid/news/2020-07-03-another-match-another-record-sergio-ramos-marks-his-450th-la-liga-appearance-for-real-mad/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The win over Getafe was Ramos's 450th La Liga appearance as a Real Madrid player, becoming just the fifth player to reach this milestone.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos scores on his 450th LaLiga appearance for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/02/ramos-scores-on-his-450th-laliga-appearance-for-real-madrid|access-date=4 July 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062549/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/02/ramos-scores-on-his-450th-laliga-appearance-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, he scored another penalty – his 22nd in a row, and his tenth goal of the season in La Liga – in a 1–0 away win over [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53298188 |title=Athletic Bilbao 0–1 Real Madrid: Sergio Ramos sends Real closer to title |work=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020 |archive-date=10 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710011621/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53298188 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37584773/real-madrid-rescued-7-10-ramos-keep-winning-run |title=Real Madrid rescued by 7/10 Ramos to keep up winning run |publisher=ESPN |last1=Kirkland |first1=Alex |date=5 July 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020 |archive-date=10 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710005710/https://www.espn.com/soccer/real-madrid/story/4127789/real-madrid-rescued-by-7-10-ramos-to-keep-up-winning-run |url-status=live }}</ref> He also became the first centre-back to score 10 goals in a La Liga season since [[Fernando Hierro]] during the [[1993–94 La Liga|1993–94]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://futaa.com/ug/article/209963/sergio-ramos-penalty-sends-real-madrid-seven-points-clear |title=Sergio Ramos' penalty sends Real Madrid seven points clear at the top of LaLiga |website=futaa |date=5 July 2020 |access-date=5 July 2020 |archive-date=6 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706005614/https://futaa.com/ug/article/209963/sergio-ramos-penalty-sends-real-madrid-seven-points-clear |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 19 July, Ramos scored his eleventh league goal in Real Madrid's last La Liga game of the season against Leganes in an eventual 2–2 draw, making it his most prolific season in White with 13 goals across all competitions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leganés-Real Madrid: 2–2: The LaLiga champions end the season with a draw|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/19/2-2-the-laliga-champions-end-the-season-with-a-draw|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062602/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/07/19/2-2-the-laliga-champions-end-the-season-with-a-draw|url-status=live}}</ref> At the end of the season, Ramos won his fifth league title with Los Blancos and Real Madrid's 34th overall.<ref name=Liga>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July ====2020–21: Final season at Real Madrid====
On 27 September 2020, Ramos opened his goal count for the season after netting the winning goal against Real Betis from the penalty spot at [[Estadio Benito Villamarín|Benito Villamarín]] in a 3–2 league win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Real Betis-Real Madrid: 2–3: Real Madrid take all three points at the Villamarín|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/09/26/2-3-real-madrid-take-all-three-points-at-the-villamarin|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090120/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/09/26/2-3-real-madrid-take-all-three-points-at-the-villamarin|url-status=live}}</ref> One month later on 24 October in El Clasico, Ramos earned and converted a penalty at the Camp Nou in a 3–1 league win – this was his 25th consecutive penalty goal for both club and country (including shoot-outs).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Barcelona-Real Madrid: 1–3: Superb win in the Clásico|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/24/1-3--superb-win-in-the-clasico|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=25 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221025045134/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/24/1-3--superb-win-in-the-clasico|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=30 October 2020|title=Sergio Ramos, 25 not out: Transmits confidence and leadership when he places the ball on the penalty spot|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/10/30/5f9c668b46163fb6128b45ad.html|access-date=2 November 2020|website=MARCA in English|language=en|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090214/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/10/30/5f9c668b46163fb6128b45ad.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos's fifth El Clasico goal equaled the record of Ronald Koeman (who was in the other dugout as manager) as the defenders with the most goals in this historic fixture. This was also Ramos's 31st consecutive La Liga Clasico, meaning he has not missed one since joining Los Blancos in 2005 – equalling Raúl and Paco Gento as the players who played in the most league Clasicos.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos nets at the Camp Nou and he equals record for LaLiga Clásico appearances|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/24/ramos-nets-at-the-camp-nou-and-he-equals-record-for-laliga-clasico-appearances|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090232/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/24/ramos-nets-at-the-camp-nou-and-he-equals-record-for-laliga-clasico-appearances|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Ramos played his first [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match of the season against [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], assisting Casemiro's 93rd minute equaliser in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mönchengladbach-Real Madrid: 2–2: Madrid draw in Germany|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/27/2-2-madrid-draw-in-germany|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090245/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/27/2-2-madrid-draw-in-germany|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's 16th Champions League campaign with Real Madrid, equalling the record of club legend, and former captain and teammate Iker Casillas.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos draws level with Casillas at top of club rankings for European Cup campaigns|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/27/ramos-draws-level-with-casillas-at-top-of-club-rankings-for-european-cup-campaigns|access-date=28 October 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090301/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/27/ramos-draws-level-with-casillas-at-top-of-club-rankings-for-european-cup-campaigns|url-status=live}}</ref> On 31 October, Ramos became just the tenth player to play 500 La Liga matches (461 for Real Madrid and 39 for Sevilla), as Madrid beat [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] 4–1 at the Alfredo Di Stefano Stadium.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sergio Ramos has now made the fourth most league appearances for Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/31/sergio-ramos-has-now-made-the-fourth-most-league-appearances-for-real-madrid|access-date=2 November 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=4 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090349/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/10/31/sergio-ramos-has-now-made-the-fourth-most-league-appearances-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 3 November, Ramos scored his 100th goal for Real Madrid in all competitions, in a 3–2 win over [[Inter Milan]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/sergio-ramos-100-real-madrid-goals/1jara3o41f8p81uvwv8bsfn4qq |title=Sergio Ramos nets 100th Real Madrid goal with Inter strike in Champions League |website=Goal.com |date=3 November 2020 |access-date=4 November 2020 |archive-date=4 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104090428/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/sergio-ramos-100-real-madrid-goals/1jara3o41f8p81uvwv8bsfn4qq |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 14 January, Ramos reportedly took four pain killer injections to his left knee to play against Athletic Bilbao in the [[2020–21 Supercopa de España#Matches#Semi-finals|2020–21 Supercopa de España semi-final]] which Real Madrid went on to lose 2–1.<ref>{{Cite web|date=15 January 2021|title=Ramos took pain killers to play in Supercopa as alarm bells ring at Real Madrid|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/01/15/600187cf46163f40178b456f.html|access-date=18 March 2021|website=MARCA in English|language=en|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061043/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/01/15/600187cf46163f40178b456f.html|url-status=live}}</ref> This was the last match Ramos would play before opting for a mid-season surgery for the first time in his career for a torn meniscus in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sergio Ramos: Real Madrid captain undergoes surgery to left knee after meniscus injury|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/12210289/sergio-ramos-real-madrid-captain-undergoes-surgery-to-left-knee-after-meniscus-injury|access-date=18 March 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061046/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11835/12210289/sergio-ramos-real-madrid-captain-undergoes-surgery-to-left-knee-after-meniscus-injury|url-status=live}}</ref> He was expected to be out for two months and to return in early April, but after a speedy recovery, Ramos started against [[Elche CF|Elche]] on 13 March – just over a month after he went under the knife.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 March 2021|title=Real Madrid 2-1 Elche: result, summary, goals|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/13/football/1615642821_744941.html|access-date=18 March 2021|website=AS.com|language=en|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718062543/https://en.as.com/en/2021/03/13/football/1615642821_744941.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Real Madrid's 2–1 win over Elche was Ramos's 334th La Liga win (315 with Real Madrid and 19 with Sevilla), equalling the record of Iker Casillas as the players with second–most wins in the Spanish top flight – only behind Messi.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ramos equals Casillas record as the player with the second most wins in LaLiga history|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/03/13/ramos-equals-casillas-record-as-the-player-with-the-second-most-wins-in-laliga-history|access-date=18 March 2021|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718074121/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/03/13/ramos-equals-casillas-record-as-the-player-with-the-second-most-wins-in-laliga-history|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Ramos played in a Champions League round of 16-second leg for the first time in three years as Real Madrid went on to defeat [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] 3–1 at the Alfredo di Stefano (5–3 on aggregate) and qualified for the quarter-finals for the first time since their last Champions League winning campaign in 2018. Ramos scored his 19th consecutive penalty for Madrid in the 60th minute which killed the game, before coming off as a substitute.<ref>{{Cite web|title=3-1: On to the Champions League quarter-finals|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/03/16/3-1-on-to-the-champions-league-quarter-finals|access-date=18 March 2021|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=18 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718061040/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/03/16/3-1-on-to-the-champions-league-quarter-finals|url-status=live}}</ref> This was Ramos's 15th Champions League goal, equalling [[Gerard Piqué]] and former teammate [[Iván Helguera]] as the second highest scoring defenders in the history of the competition – with only former teammate [[Roberto Carlos]] ahead of them.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 March 2021|title=Highest scoring defenders ever including United legend, as Ramos hits 101st for Real|url=https://talksport.com/football/473669/highest-scoring-defenders-sergio-ramos-100-goal-real-madrid-barcelona-man-utd/|access-date=18 March 2021|website=talkSPORT|language=en-US|archive-date=24 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524173209/https://talksport.com/football/473669/highest-scoring-defenders-sergio-ramos-100-goal-real-madrid-barcelona-man-utd/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Due to an injury, Ramos missed his first El Clásico since joining Real Madrid, ending a streak of playing in 31 consecutive league Clásicos.<ref>{{Cite web|date=1 April 2021|title=This is how Sergio Ramos got injured|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/01/6065d2cd22601ddb758b45f0.html|access-date=11 April 2021|website=Marca|location=Spain|language=en|archive-date=10 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510060857/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/01/6065d2cd22601ddb758b45f0.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He later missed the second leg of the Champions League quarter-finals against Liverpool, as he tested positive for [[COVID-19]], although he was also injured.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/13/607566afe2704e79308b45f9.html |title=Sergio Ramos tests positive for COVID-19 |website=Marca |date=13 April 2021 |access-date=19 April 2021 |archive-date=22 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210622114710/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/13/607566afe2704e79308b45f9.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 5 May, in the Champions League semi-final second leg against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], his side lost 2–0 and were eliminated from the competition; however, he then sustained an injury in his left [[hamstring]] which forced him to miss the rest of the season; this meant he had played his last game for Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/05/08/609665e746163fd8498b45eb.html |title=Sergio Ramos is injured again: Goodbye to Real Madrid? |website=Marca |date=8 May 2021 |access-date=8 May 2021 |archive-date=30 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210730165922/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/05/08/609665e746163fd8498b45eb.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Ramos played just 21 matches for Los Blancos in 2020–21, making it his most injury-riddled season, after having played at least 33 matches in each of his previous 15 campaigns at the club.<ref>{{Cite web|date=24 May 2021|title=Sergio Ramos' hardest year|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/05/25/60ac1ced268e3edc258b457b.html|access-date=26 May 2021|website=MARCA|language=en|archive-date=4 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210804072306/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/05/25/60ac1ced268e3edc258b457b.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 June, Real Madrid announced that Ramos would leave the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=16 June 2021|title=Official announcement|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/16/official-announcement|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=16 June 2021|archive-date=16 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616194105/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/16/official-announcement|url-status=live}}</ref> During his farewell event on the next day, Ramos, who had initially asked for a two-year offer, mentioned that he accepted a one-year contract renewal with a salary reduction; however, the offer had expired without his knowledge.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/06/17/60cb3e89ca47415a698b45a8.html |title=Sergio Ramos: When I accepted Real Madrid's renewal offer, it no longer existed |website=MARCA |date=17 June 2021 |access-date=17 June 2021 |archive-date=29 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629002734/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/06/17/60cb3e89ca47415a698b45a8.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Paris Saint-Germain ===
[[File:Sergio Ramos & Vitinha (PSG 2023).jpg|thumb|Ramos (centre, in white) playing for [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2023]]

==== 2021–22: Various injuries and Ligue 1 title ====
On 8 July 2021, it was announced that Ramos had signed a two-year contract with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].<ref>{{cite web|date=8 July 2021|title=Sergio Ramos signs with Paris Saint-Germain|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/sergio-ramos-signs-with-paris-saint-germain-until-2023|website=psg.fr|access-date=8 July 2021|archive-date=11 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711180231/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/sergio-ramos-signs-with-paris-saint-germain-until-2023|url-status=live}}</ref> He chose to wear the number 4 jersey, with [[Thilo Kehrer]] switching to the number 24 shirt.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=No.4 for Ramos!|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/no4-for-ramos-psg-equipe-premiere-sergio-ramos|access-date=9 July 2021|website=EN.PSG.FR|date=8 July 2021 |language=en|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709190515/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/no4-for-ramos-psg-equipe-premiere-sergio-ramos|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos remarked: "I am quite superstitious about it and I love the number 4 because I have worn that number since the start of my career and it has followed me throughout my career and my life, bringing with me much luck and many victories".<ref name=":0" /> During the medical examination required to complete the signing, the medical staff at PSG were reported to be impressed by his seriousness and physique, whilst the medical results were noted to be excellent and incredible.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PSG - Sergio Ramos a impressionné le staff à la visite médicale|url=https://www.madeinparisiens.com/mercato-psg/article-psg-sergio-ramos-a-impressionne-le-staff-a-la-visite-medicale-348473.html|access-date=9 July 2021|website=Madeinparisiens.com|date=7 July 2021 |language=fr|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709191441/https://www.madeinparisiens.com/mercato-psg/article-psg-sergio-ramos-a-impressionne-le-staff-a-la-visite-medicale-348473.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=PSG : 'Les tests médicaux de Ramos sont incroyables' révèle Bouhafsi|date=7 July 2021 |url=https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/psg-les-tests-medicaux-de-ramos-sont-incroyables-revele-bouhafsi_VN-202107070408.html|language=fr|access-date=9 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709191439/https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/psg-les-tests-medicaux-de-ramos-sont-incroyables-revele-bouhafsi_VN-202107070408.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The staff compared Ramos's physique to that of a 25-year-old (he was 35 at the time).<ref>{{Cite web|date=9 July 2021|title=Ramos 'like a 25-year-old' as he signs for PSG|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/ligue-1/2021/07/09/60e88a24268e3ea3458b45a0.html|access-date=9 July 2021|website=MARCA|language=en|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709175227/https://www.marca.com/en/football/ligue-1/2021/07/09/60e88a24268e3ea3458b45a0.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Due to a series of injury problems, Ramos made his first appearance in a match day squad for Paris Saint-Germain ahead of a Champions League group stage game against Manchester City on 24 November 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sergio Ramos finally in first PSG squad for Man City trip|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-finally-in-first-psg-squad-for-man-city-trip-34121001|access-date=23 November 2021|website=OneFootball|archive-date=23 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123171535/https://onefootball.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-finally-in-first-psg-squad-for-man-city-trip-34121001|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut four days later in a 3–1 league victory over [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.goal.com/br/not%C3%ADcias/sergio-ramos-coloca-fim-ao-seu-calvario-e-estreia-pelo-psg/bltdb0a0574d083b2fc| title = Sergio Ramos coloca fim ao seu calvário e estreia pelo PSG| publisher = Goal| date = 28 November 2021| access-date = 28 November 2021| archive-date = 28 November 2021| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211128140358/https://www.goal.com/br/not%C3%ADcias/sergio-ramos-coloca-fim-ao-seu-calvario-e-estreia-pelo-psg/bltdb0a0574d083b2fc| url-status = live}}</ref> On 23 January 2022, Sergio scored his debut goal for the club, helping PSG to beat [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] 4–0 in a home league match.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Sergio Ramos nets first Paris Saint-Germain goal in win over Reims|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/ligue-1/2021-2022/ligue-1-live_sto8728109/story.shtml|access-date=23 January 2022|website=Eurosport|archive-date=30 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030213532/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos won the [[2021–22 Ligue 1]] in his first season at the club.<ref name="Bosher2022">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4179531/2022/04/22/psg-crowned-ligue-1-champions-after-messi-secures-draw-against-lens/|title=PSG crowned Ligue 1 champions after draw against Lens|publisher=[[The Athletic]]|first1=Luke|last1=Bosher|first2=Jacob|last2=Whitehead|date=23 April 2022|access-date=23 April 2022|archive-date=1 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601050533/https://theathletic.com/news/psg-crowned-ligue-1-champions-after-messi-secures-draw-against-lens/aoDgDkRZDFEo/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2022–23: Last season at PSG ====
PSG started the 2022–23 season by winning the [[2022 Trophée des Champions]] in [[Tel Aviv]], in which Ramos scored a goal in a 4–0 win over [[FC Nantes|Nantes]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Rooke |first=Sam |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/trophee-des-champions/2022-2023/trophee-des-champions-2022-psg-v-nantes-follow-live-coverage_sto9066708/story.shtml |title=Paris Saint-Germain 4-0 Nantes: Lionel Messi, Neymar and Sergio Ramos goals help PSG win Trophée des Champions |publisher=Eurosport |date=31 July 2022 |access-date=18 March 2023 |archive-date=9 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209050151/https://www.eurosport.com/football/trophee-des-champions/2022-2023/trophee-des-champions-2022-psg-v-nantes-follow-live-coverage_sto9066708/story.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> On 6 September 2022, he made his Champions League debut with Paris Saint-Germain in a 2–1 win over Juventus.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/match/2022/sep/06/parisstgermain-v-juventus |title=PSG 2–1 Juventus |work=The Guardian |date=6 September 2022 |access-date=18 March 2023 |archive-date=18 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318222941/https://www.theguardian.com//football/match/2022/sep/06/parisstgermain-v-juventus |url-status=live }}</ref> On 8 February 2023, in a 1-2 defeat against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in the [[Coupe de France]], he score a header to become at 36 years and 315 days PSG’s oldest goalscorer ever.<ref> {{cite web |title=OM - PSG : incroyable record pour Sergio Ramos ! |url=https://www.onzemondial.com/coupe-de-france/om-psg-incroyable-record-pour-sergio-ramos-819409 |website=Onze Mondial |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>
On 8 April 2023, he scored against [[OGC Nice|Nice]] at 37 years and 9 days to become Paris Saint-Germain’s oldest Ligue 1 goalscorer.<ref> {{cite web |title=PSG : Sergio Ramos s'est offert un record à Nice |url=https://www.butfootballclub.fr/150789-psg-ramos-s-est-offert-un-record-a-nice-813923/ |website=But Football Club |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>
On 2 June 2023, Ramos announced that he would be leaving PSG at the end of the season, following the expiration of his contract on 30 June.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2023 |title=Sergio Ramos, a true champion |url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/sergio-ramos-a-true-champion-paris-saint-germain-2022-2023 |access-date=3 June 2023 |website=EN.PSG.FR |language=en |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603000525/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/sergio-ramos-a-true-champion-paris-saint-germain-2022-2023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/sergio-ramos-un-sacre-champion-paris-saint-germain-2022-2023|title=Sergio Ramos, un sacré champion|language=fr|publisher=Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|date=2 June 2023|access-date=2 June 2023|archive-date=2 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602204119/https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/sergio-ramos-un-sacre-champion-paris-saint-germain-2022-2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 June 2023 |title=Sergio Ramos to leave PSG at end of season |url=https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/37782612/sergio-ramos-leave-psg-final-game-season |access-date=3 June 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en |archive-date=2 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602230240/https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/37782612/sergio-ramos-leave-psg-final-game-season |url-status=live }}</ref> One day later, he opened the score in a 2–3 defeat against [[Clermont Foot|Clermont]] in his last appearance for the club as Paris Saint-Germain won their record 11th Ligue 1 title.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Gill |title=WATCH: Sergio Ramos heads PSG in front against Clermont in final appearance for PSG |url=https://www.goal.com/en-cm/news/watch-sergio-ramos-scores-psg-final-appearance/blt7a4cafd0f70fa10a |website=Goal.com |access-date=3 June 2023 |date=3 June 2023 |archive-date=3 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230603213402/https://www.goal.com/en-cm/news/watch-sergio-ramos-scores-psg-final-appearance/blt7a4cafd0f70fa10a |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Return to Sevilla ===
On 4 September 2023, Ramos returned to his boyhood club Sevilla after 18 years, signing a contract until the end of the [[2023–24 Sevilla FC season|season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 September 2023 |title=Sergio Ramos returns to Sevilla FC after 18 years |url=https://www.sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/sergio-ramos-signs-2324 |access-date=4 September 2023 |website=Sevilla FC |language=en |archive-date=4 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904163215/https://www.sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/sergio-ramos-signs-2324 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 17 September, he made his second debut for Sevilla in a 1–0 win over Las Palmas at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/sevilla/2023/09/17/6506228fca47412a1b8b459c.html |title=Sergio Ramos, titular ante Las Palmas |publisher=Marca |language=es |date=17 September 2023 |access-date=17 September 2023 |archive-date=3 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003212115/https://www.marca.com/futbol/sevilla/2023/09/17/6506228fca47412a1b8b459c.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/resultados/futbol/primera/2023_2024/directo/regular_a_5_441139/ |title=Sevilla 1–0 Las Palmas |publisher=as.com |date=17 September 2023 |access-date=17 September 2023 |archive-date=3 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003212117/https://en.as.com/resultados/futbol/primera/2023_2024/directo/regular_a_5_441139/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Three days later, he made his [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut with Sevilla in a 1–1 draw against [[RC Lens|Lens]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/sevilla-lens-champions-league-5914cc8cf836e79cac2a0c32bf9eec70 |title=Sevilla held by Lens 1-1 at home in group stage of Champions League |publisher=AP News |date=20 September 2023 |access-date=20 September 2023 |archive-date=21 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230921130853/https://apnews.com/article/sevilla-lens-champions-league-5914cc8cf836e79cac2a0c32bf9eec70 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 21 October, Ramos played against his former club Real Madrid for the first time since he left in 2021, in a La Liga match that ended in a 1–1 draw at the Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium, helping secure a point from the match.<ref>{{Cite news |date=21 October 2023 |title=Sevilla 1-1 Real Madrid: Sergio Ramos helps Sevilla hold his old team |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67184428 |access-date=23 October 2023 |archive-date=23 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231023000816/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67184428 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 26 November, he was involved in a notable and bizarre incident during a match against [[Real Sociedad]], in which he received two red cards. He was initially shown a red card after receiving a second yellow card for a late challenge on [[Brais Méndez]]. Following this, he appealed for a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] review, prompting the referee to examine the slow-motion footage. After reviewing the footage, the referee rescinded the second yellow card, and immediately issued Ramos a straight red card.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/1656534/sergio-ramos-reaction-two-red-cards-sevilla/ |title=Footage catches Sergio Ramos being left speechless to bizarre moment he is shown TWO red cards... |publisher=talkSPORT |date=27 November 2023 |access-date=1 November 2024 |archive-date=28 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128141820/https://talksport.com/football/1656534/sergio-ramos-reaction-two-red-cards-sevilla/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 29 November, he scored his first goal for Sevilla following his return in a 3–2 home defeat against [[PSV Eindhoven]] in the Champions League, equaling the record of most goals scored by defenders set by Roberto Carlos and Gerard Piqué, which also marked the 10,000th goal in the competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67573014 |title=Sevilla 2–3 PSV Eindhoven |publisher=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2023 |access-date=30 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725130040/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67573014 |archive-date=25 July 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://getfootballnewsspain.com/sergio-ramos-equals-gerard-pique-and-roberto-carlos-in-champions-league-record-books/ |title=Sergio Ramos equals Gerard Piqué and Roberto Carlos in Champions League record books |publisher=Get Spanish Football News |date=29 November 2023 |access-date=1 December 2023 |archive-date=25 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240225064442/https://getfootballnewsspain.com/sergio-ramos-equals-gerard-pique-and-roberto-carlos-in-champions-league-record-books/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 12 December, he broke the record, by scoring his 17th goal with a Panenka-style penalty in a 2–1 away defeat against Lens.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-makes-champions-league-history-in-some-style-38714646 |title=Sergio Ramos makes Champions League history in some style |publisher=OneFootball |date=12 December 2023 |access-date=13 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231213014208/https://onefootball.com/en/news/sergio-ramos-makes-champions-league-history-in-some-style-38714646 |archive-date=13 December 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 25 February 2024, Ramos returned to the Santiago Bernabéu to play against Real Madrid, following his departure from the club in 2021, as his team suffered a 1–0 defeat.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 February 2024 |title=Modric scores sublime late winner for Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68373528 |access-date=26 February 2024 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=25 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240225181823/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68373528 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later that year, on 17 June, Sevilla announced that Ramos would not stay at the club for the following season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sergio Ramos no seguirá en el Sevilla |url=https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/sergio-ramos-no-seguira-sevilla-fc |website=Sevilla FC |access-date=17 June 2024 |date=17 June 2024 |language=es |archive-date=17 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617114702/https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/sergio-ramos-no-seguira-sevilla-fc |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Monterrey===
On 6 February 2025, Ramos was announced as a new player for [[Liga MX]] side [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]], after various days of speculation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 February 2025 |title=WELCOME TO RAYADOS, SERGIO RAMOS! |url=https://www.rayados.com/en/news/20473/welcome-to-rayados-sergio-ramos |access-date=13 February 2025 |publisher=[[C.F. Monterrey|Club de Fútbol Monterrey Rayados]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260710234329/https://www.rayados.com/en/news/20473/welcome-to-rayados-sergio-ramos |archive-date=10 July 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid legend Sergio Ramos signs for Liga MX's Monterrey|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/43641717/real-madrid-legend-sergio-ramos-signs-liga-mx-monterrey|publisher=ESPN|language=English|date=6 February 2025|access-date=6 February 2025|archive-date=7 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207111928/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/43641717/real-madrid-legend-sergio-ramos-signs-liga-mx-monterrey|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos chose to wear number 93 instead of his traditional number 4 to honor his 93rd-minute equaliser in the [[2014 UEFA Champions League final]] for Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sergio Ramos will play for Monterrey in Liga MX with 93 on his back as a nod to the goal that he scored for Real Madrid in the 2014 Champions League final.|url=https://www.kget.com/sports/sports-illustrated/6c75d29e/why-is-sergio-ramos-wearing-number-93-for-monterrey-in-liga-mx/|publisher=SportsIllustrated|language=English|date=7 February 2025|access-date=7 February 2025}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Ramos was handed the captain's armband on his debut for the club against [[Atlético San Luis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/sergio-ramos-makes-debut-as-monterrey-cruise-past-san-luis-1348987 |title=Sergio Ramos makes debut as Monterrey cruise past San Luis |publisher=BeSoccer |date=23 February 2025 }} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> On 3 March, he scored his first goal for the club in a 4–2 victory over [[Santos Laguna]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c62z8njwdq0o |title=Ramos scores first Monterrey goal; free tickets for Messi no-show |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 March 2025 |access-date=4 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723173800/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c62z8njwdq0o |archive-date=23 July 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 17 March 2025, he was sent off for the 30th time in his career (first with Monterrey) after receiving a straight red card for kicking [[Club Universidad Nacional|UNAM]]'s striker [[Guillermo Martínez (footballer)|Guillermo Martínez]] from behind after failing to steal the ball.<ref>{{cite web |last=Conrad |first=Alex |date=17 March 2025 |title=Sergio Ramos jokes after getting 30th red card of his career for booting opponent. |url=https://talksport.com/football/3028090/sergio-ramos-sent-off-reaction-monterrey/ |access-date=11 April 2025 |publisher=talkSPORT}}</ref> Later that year, on 18 June, he scored the opening goal in a 1–1 draw against Inter Milan during the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]], being also named Man of the Match.<ref name=Temb>{{cite web |url=https://tembah.net/en/news?nid=70988 |title=Ramos makes Club World Cup history |website=tembah.net |date=18 June 2025 |access-date=22 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250707231344/https://tembah.net/en/news?nid=70988 |archive-date=7 July 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> In doing so at the age of 39 years and 80 days old, he became the oldest player in history to score in the Club World Cup, breaking the previous record set by [[Javier Zanetti]] in the [[2010 FIFA Club World Cup|2010 edition]] at the age of 37.<ref name=Temb/> In December of that year, he announced his departure from the club following the conclusion of his contract, becoming a free agent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/47258351/spain-great-sergio-ramos-confirms-not-renew-liga-mx-monterrey |title=Sergio Ramos confirms he will not renew with Liga MX's Monterrey |publisher=ESPN |date=9 December 2025 |access-date=10 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714065554/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/47258351/spain-great-sergio-ramos-confirms-not-renew-liga-mx-monterrey |archive-date=14 July 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
===2002–2006: Youth level and early international career===
In 2004, Ramos became an instant hit for [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain's under-19]], for whom he played six international matches. During the [[2004 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2004 U19 Euro]], Ramos was a key figure for Spain as he started in four out of five of their matches on the way to winning their second U19 European Championship, including scoring a decisive penalty in the Semi-final penalty-shoot out against [[Ukraine national under-19 football team|Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=UEFA European U-19 Championship|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/under19/history/season=2004/round=1665/match=79220/index.html|website=archive.is|date=5 January 2013|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130105021937/http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/under19/history/season=2004/round=1665/match=79220/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/under19/history/season=2004/round=1666/match=79251/index.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715082459/http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/under19/history/season=2004/round=1666/match=79251/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 July 2012|title=UEFA European U-19 C'ship|date=15 July 2012|website=archive.is|access-date=1 March 2019}}</ref> On 26 March 2005, in a 3–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win over [[China national football team|China]] in [[Salamanca]], he first appeared for the [[Spain national football team|senior side]] at only 18 years and 361 days of age, making him the youngest player to play for the national team in the last 55 years.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Selección española Sergio Ramos, un devorador de récords que no tiene techo|url=https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20201112/sergio-ramos-devorador-records-no-tiene-techo/2055551.shtml|website=[[RTVE]]|date=12 November 2020|access-date=27 May 2024|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240527121553/https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20201112/sergio-ramos-devorador-records-no-tiene-techo/2055551.shtml|archive-date=27 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> He held this record until 1 March 2006, when it was broken by [[Cesc Fàbregas]] in a friendly match against [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2005/03/27/pagina-4/1309544/pdf.html|title=Aperitivo oriental|trans-title=Oriental hors d'oeuvre|work=[[El Mundo Deportivo (newspaper)|El Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=27 March 2005|access-date=17 May 2013|archive-date=23 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923103450/http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2005/03/27/pagina-4/1309544/pdf.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 12 October 2005, Ramos scored his first two international goals in a 6–0 away thrashing of [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Torres towers in Spain win|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/01ae-0f847b010cf5-e14249117e52-1000--torres-towers-in-spain-win/|publisher=UEFA|date=12 October 2005|archive-date=23 March 2025|access-date=23 March 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250323045443/https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/01ae-0f847b010cf5-e14249117e52-1000--torres-towers-in-spain-win/|url-status=live}}</ref> He was selected for the final stages in Germany and, after the international retirement of Real Madrid teammate [[Míchel Salgado]], became the undisputed first-choice right-back. Despite wearing the number 4 jersey for Real Madrid, Ramos admitted he wears the number 15 for Spain in memory of his close friend and former Sevilla teammate Puerta, who died in August 2007 and made his Spain debut wearing No. 15.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/es-ar/noticias/el-homenaje-a-su-amigo-por-que-sergio-ramos-usa-el-dorsal-15/faeqoyu3re1t186ocmnouke2m|title=El homenaje a su amigo Antonio Puerta: Por qué Sergio Ramos usa el dorsal 15 en la Selección de España|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=es|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=3 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603074734/https://www.goal.com/es-ar/noticias/el-homenaje-a-su-amigo-por-que-sergio-ramos-usa-el-dorsal-15/faeqoyu3re1t186ocmnouke2m|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/6964586.stm|title=Sevilla's Puerta dies in hospital|date=28 August 2007|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=22 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822183649/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/6964586.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2008–2012: Spain's Golden Generation===
[[File:Sergio Ramos Euro 2012 vs France 02.jpg|thumb|Ramos at the [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]], in a [[UEFA Euro 2012 knockout phase#Spain vs France|quarter-final match against France]].]]

Throughout Spain's [[UEFA Euro 2008]] [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|qualifying campaign]], Ramos was a regular member of the starting eleven as the national side finished first in its group, above [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]]. He scored two goals, including one in a 3–1 away win over [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]], in 11 appearances. In the tournament's final stages, Ramos played in all matches and minutes, except the 2–1 group stage win against [[Greece national football team|Greece]]. In [[UEFA Euro 2008 Final|the final]], his pass nearly set up [[Marcos Senna]]'s first international goal, but the latter missed his opportunity by inches. During the celebrations after the 1–0 defeat of [[Germany national football team|Germany]], he wore a T-shirt in honour of his late friend Puerta.<ref>[http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202738775658/noticia/Noticia/Ramos_pays_tribute_to_Antonio_Puerta.htm Ramos pays tribute to Antonio Puerta] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101006183142/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202738775658/noticia/Noticia/Ramos_pays_tribute_to_Antonio_Puerta.htm |date=6 October 2010 }}; Real Madrid CF, 30 June 2008</ref>

Ramos was selected in the squad for the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in South Africa, as Spain finished in third.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090701011016/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/matches/round=250121/match=66212/index.html#nosticky FIFA Confederations Cup South Africa 2009];FIFA.com, 28 June 2009</ref> On 3 June 2010, he captained Spain for the first time, in a 1–0 friendly win over [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] in [[Innsbruck]], Austria.<ref>{{cite news|title=1–0. Un chutazo de Navas derrota a Corea del Sur|trans-title=1–0. A blast from Navas defeats South Korea|url=http://segoviaaldia.es/not/2618/|access-date=7 September 2015|publisher=Segovia al Día|date=3 June 2010|language=es|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304121256/http://segoviaaldia.es/not/2618/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]], held in the same country, Ramos played every minute of the tournament as a right back, helping Spain keep five [[Shutout|clean sheets]] and reach [[2010 FIFA World Cup Final|the final]], which they won 1–0 against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]; he topped the tournament's [[Castrol Performance Index]] with a score of 9.79.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/2292/editorials/2010/07/12/2022035/spains-sergio-ramos-tops-2010-world-cup-castrol-index Spain's Sergio Ramos tops 2010 World Cup Castrol Index] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100724065840/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/2292/editorials/2010/07/12/2022035/spains-sergio-ramos-tops-2010-world-cup-castrol-index |date=24 July 2010 }}; Goal.com, 12 July 2010</ref> Despite playing at right-back, he also completed more [[Dribbling#Association football|solo runs]] than any other player in the tournament, 31.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/spain-s-2010-conquerors-in-numbers-2904843 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180607103350/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/spain-s-2010-conquerors-in-numbers-2904843 |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 June 2018 |title=Spain's 2010 conquerors in numbers |publisher=FIFA |date=22 August 2017 |access-date=18 May 2020 }}</ref>

[[File:Torres, Mata and Ramos Euro 2012 trophy 01.jpg|thumb|[[Fernando Torres]] (left), [[Juan Mata]] (centre), and Ramos (right) holding the [[Henri Delaunay Trophy]] after winning the [[UEFA Euro 2012]].]]
Ramos returned to the heart of the defence for [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]]. When asked about his role change, he replied: "I have adapted and feel comfortable in the middle, but I am a World and European champion at right-back".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2012/02/27/2933478/sergio-ramos-i-have-adapted-to-play-as-a-center-back-forl=|title=Sergio Ramos: I have adapted to play as a centre-back for Spain|work=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=28 February 2012|access-date=1 June 2012|archive-date=21 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021005251/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2012/02/27/2933478/sergio-ramos-i-have-adapted-to-play-as-a-center-back-forl=|url-status=live}}</ref> He played all the games in [[Poland]] and [[Ukraine]] alongside Barcelona's [[Gerard Piqué]] and, in the semi-finals against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]], he converted his penalty shootout attempt in an eventual 4–2 win (0–0 after 120 minutes), scoring for the eventual champions in [[Antonín Panenka|Panenka]]-style.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0252-0cdc4f07099d-bbe9e9886641-1000--spain-survive-test-of-nerve-against-portugal-to-reach-euro-/|title=Spain survive test of nerve to reach final|publisher=UEFA|date=27 June 2012|access-date=28 June 2012|archive-date=28 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190928052011/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2012/matches/round=15174/match=2003378/postmatch/report/index.html#spain+survive+test+nerve+reach+final|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 July, Ramos won his third trophy with the Spanish senior National Team as they thrashed Italy 4–0 in the final. Ramos's performances during the Euro earned him a place in the Team of The Tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/memories/newsid=2325815.html|title=UEFA EURO 2016 – History|website=[[UEFA]]|date=23 May 2016|language=en|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=3 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303050416/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/memories/newsid=2325815.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ramos wore another T-shirt during Spain's Euro 2012 celebrations to pay homage to his late friend Puerta.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/orgullodenervion/noticias/sevilla-fc/ramos-navas-puerta-eurocopa-final.html|title=Ramos y Navas rinden homenaje a Puerta|website=Orgullo de Nervión|date=July 2012|language=es-ES|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=1 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901010435/https://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/orgullodenervion/noticias/sevilla-fc/ramos-navas-puerta-eurocopa-final.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2013–2019: Assuming the captaincy===
[[File:Hector ramos vs Spain.jpg|thumb|Ramos (in red) in action for Spain in a game against [[Puerto Rico national football team|Puerto Rico]].]]
On 22 March 2013, Ramos celebrated his 100th [[Cap (sport)|cap]] by opening the scoring in a 1–1 draw with [[Finland national football team|Finland]] in [[Gijón]] for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2014 World Cup qualifiers]]. He became the youngest European player ever to reach that figure in the process, surpassing Germany's [[Lukas Podolski]].<ref name=Young>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/03/22/futbol/seleccion/1363987482.html|title=Ramos: centenario, capitán y goleador|trans-title=Ramos: 100th game, captain and scorer|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=22 March 2013|access-date=23 March 2013|archive-date=21 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621043000/http://www.marca.com/2013/03/22/futbol/seleccion/1363987482.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In June, Ramos contested in the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in Brazil, starting every match as Spain lost to the hosts in [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Final|the final]]. He captained the side for their second [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Final|group]] game, a 10–0 win over [[Tahiti national football team|Tahiti]] at the [[Maracanã Stadium|Maracanã]], which is the biggest win of his career.<ref>{{cite news|title=Spain go for jugular against tiny Tahiti|url=http://www.egyptindependent.com/news/spain-go-jugular-against-tiny-tahiti|access-date=7 July 2015|agency=Agence France-Presse|work=Egypt Independent|date=21 June 2013|archive-date=7 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307090017/http://www.egyptindependent.com//news/spain-go-jugular-against-tiny-tahiti|url-status=live}}</ref> On 30 June, he missed a penalty kick in the 3–0 [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Final|Confederations Cup Final]] loss to [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/30/brazil-spain-live-confederations-cup-final|title=Brazil v Spain: Confederations Cup final – as it happened|date=30 June 2013|work=The Guardian|access-date=13 December 2016|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618075803/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/30/brazil-spain-live-confederations-cup-final|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ramos was selected for his third [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27647635|title=World Cup 2014: Spain drop Alvaro Negredo and Jesus Navas|work=BBC Sport|date=31 May 2014|access-date=31 May 2014|archive-date=1 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140601200444/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/27647635|url-status=live}}</ref> He played the full 90 minutes of each of the team's matches in Brazil, each with a different partner in central defence, as the reigning champions were eliminated from the group stage.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Ornstein|first1=David|title=Spain 1–5 Netherlands|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285043|access-date=28 June 2016|work=BBC Sport|date=13 June 2014|archive-date=24 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170624163355/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285043|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Ornstein|first1=David|title=Spain 0–2 Chile|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285155|access-date=28 June 2016|work=BBC Sport|date=18 June 2014|archive-date=11 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211081752/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285155|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chowdhury|first1=Saj|title=Australia 0–3 Spain|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285263|access-date=28 June 2016|work=BBC Sport|date=23 June 2014|archive-date=4 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404150055/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285263|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Russia-Spain 2017 (1).jpg|thumb|Ramos celebrates after scoring a goal against [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in a friendly in [[Saint Petersburg]].]]

In February 2016, Ramos won the [[Luis Aragonés]] Award by [[Marca (newspaper)|''Marca'']], which distinguished him as the best player of the national team in the past year.<ref name="Navarro2016">{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/02/sergio-ramos-recognised-as-the-spanish-national-teams-best-player|title=Sergio Ramos, recognised as the Spain national team's best player|publisher=Real Madrid CF|author=Alberto Navarro|date=8 February 2016|access-date=15 March 2020|archive-date=25 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125115734/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/02/sergio-ramos-recognised-as-the-spanish-national-teams-best-player|url-status=live}}</ref> With [[David de Gea]] selected ahead of Iker Casillas in Spain's starting line-up, Ramos captained the team at [[UEFA Euro 2016]]. On 21 June 2016, he had a penalty kick saved by [[Danijel Subašić]] in a 2–1 loss to [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36524210|title=Croatia 2–1 Spain|date=21 June 2016|publisher=BBC|access-date=13 February 2018|archive-date=22 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622003022/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36524210|url-status=live}}</ref> Spain finished their Euro group as runners-up and crashed out in the Round of 16 against [[Italy national football team|Italy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2016/06/27/football/italy-spain-euro-2016/index.html|title=Spain sent crashing out of Euro 2016 by Italy|last=Masters|first=James|date=27 June 2016|publisher=CNN|access-date=7 February 2019|archive-date=24 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724045935/https://edition.cnn.com/2016/06/27/football/italy-spain-euro-2016/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 March 2018, days before turning 32, Ramos earned his 150th cap for Spain in a 1–1 friendly draw with Germany in [[Düsseldorf]]. Only [[Iker Casillas]] had previously reached the mark for the team.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Corrigan |first1=Dermot |title=Sergio Ramos reaches 150 caps for Spain: six of his best appearances |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/spain/164/blog/post/3430108/sergio-ramos-150-spain-caps-highlights-of-remarkable-international-career |access-date=9 June 2018 |publisher=ESPN |date=24 March 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612141651/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/spain/164/blog/post/3430108/sergio-ramos-150-spain-caps-highlights-of-remarkable-international-career |url-status=live }}</ref>

Ramos was included in the Spain [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] and would go into his fourth tournament, and first World Cup as Captain after Iker Casillas missed out.<ref>{{cite web|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018|archive-date=9 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709141140/https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|url-status=live}}</ref> He played in all three of Spain's Group stage matches as they topped the 'Group of Death' ahead of European Champions Portugal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/review-spain-morocco-591w-2968948|title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia - News - Spain top group after thrilling finale|website=FIFA.com|language=en-GB|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=3 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603075205/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/review-spain-morocco-591w-2968948|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[2018 FIFA World Cup#Round of 16|Round of 16]] against [[Russia national football team|Russia]], Ramos believed he scored the opening goal but it was later credited as an [[Sergei Ignashevich]] own goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://au.sports.yahoo.com/spains-sergio-ramos-slammed-despicable-celebration-224611372.html|title=Spain's Sergio Ramos slammed for 'despicable' celebration|date=July 2018 |publisher=Yahoo! Sport|language=en-AU|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=28 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728015859/https://au.sports.yahoo.com/spains-sergio-ramos-slammed-despicable-celebration-224611372.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The match ended 1–1 after extra time and was decided on penalties (4–3) as the hosts eliminated La Roja. Ramos scored Spain's fourth penalty but it wasn't enough as teammates [[Koke (footballer, born 1992)|Koke]] and [[Iago Aspas|Aspas]] both had their penalties saved.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/216814/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622165336/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/216814/|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 June 2018|title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia – Players – Sergio RAMOS|publisher=FIFA|access-date=19 July 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44591345|title=World Cup 2018: Russia reach quarter-finals after 4–3 penalty shootout win over Spain|date=1 July 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=19 July 2018|language=en-GB|archive-date=22 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210622203909/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44591345|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:ESP-RUS (2).jpg|thumb|Ramos (left, in red) with [[Russia national football team|Russia]] captain [[Igor Akinfeev]] (right, in blue) and referee [[Björn Kuipers]] before the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]] Round of 16 match at the [[Luzhniki Stadium]] in [[Moscow]].]]

With new coach [[Luis Enrique (footballer)|Luis Enrique]], Ramos retained captaincy of the national team. He played in all four of Spain's [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League]] group matches, becoming the nation's top scorer in the group with three goals – scoring once against England and twice against Croatia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefanationsleague/teams/122--spain/|title=Spain|access-date=9 November 2018|publisher=UEFA|language=en-GB|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328165850/https://www.uefa.com/uefanationsleague/season=2020/teams/team=122/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefanationsleague/teams/players/93649--sergio-ramos/statistics/|title=Sergio Ramos|access-date=9 November 2018|publisher=UEFA|language=en-GB|archive-date=17 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117110536/https://www.uefa.com/uefanationsleague/season=2019/teams/player=93649/statistics/|url-status=live}}</ref> Spain finished second in their UEFA Nations League Group, which saw them miss out on the [[2019 UEFA Nations League Finals]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/11/18/5bf19445e5fdeafe648b45c1.html|title=Spain don't make the UEFA Nations League Final Four|access-date=8 November 2018|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=en-GB|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328020411/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/11/18/5bf19445e5fdeafe648b45c1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In March 2019, Ramos scored the winner in Spain's first [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] match against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] through another [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka]] penalty in a 2–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/23/5c96a8de22601de82a8b45b7.html|title=Spain avoid Norway stumble|date=23 March 2019|website=MARCA in English|language=en|access-date=24 March 2019|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328020356/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/23/5c96a8de22601de82a8b45b7.html|url-status=live}}</ref> This was his tenth penalty of the season, scoring them all. It was also his fifth consecutive match scoring for Spain, which is a personal record.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/23/5c96b88d468aeb4d1f8b4605.html|title=Ramos further improves his records with another Panenka penalty|date=23 March 2019|website=MARCA in English|language=en|access-date=24 March 2019|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328042724/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/23/5c96b88d468aeb4d1f8b4605.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Spain manager Enrique hailed Ramos as a "unique player in history" after the match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/24/5c96bac4468aeb27038b4601.html|title=Luis Enrique: Ramos is a unique player in history|date=23 March 2019|website=MARCA in English|language=en|access-date=24 March 2019|archive-date=24 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324003958/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/03/24/5c96bac4468aeb27038b4601.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2019–2021: Record caps for Spain===
In the second Euro 2020 qualification match, away to [[Malta national football team|Malta]], Ramos did not score for the first time in six matches for Spain – failing to extend his scoring streak. However, the match ended 2–0 to Spain which was his 121st win with La Roja, equaling the all-time record of Iker Casillas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.telemadrid.es/programas/deportes-tn/Sergio-Ramos-amenaza-Casillas-2-2107309295--20190327034403.html|title=Sergio Ramos 'threatens' Casillas|website=telemadrid.es|date=27 March 2019|access-date=28 March 2019|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328033540/http://www.telemadrid.es/programas/deportes-tn/Sergio-Ramos-amenaza-Casillas-2-2107309295--20190327034403.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 June 2019, Ramos broke the record of most international victories with 122, following a 4–1 victory against the [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]], scoring Spain's opening goal in the process.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.football-espana.net/78610/sergio-ramos-breaks-international-win-record|title=Sergio Ramos breaks international win record|work=Football España|date=7 June 2019|access-date=7 June 2019|archive-date=7 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607215846/https://www.football-espana.net/78610/sergio-ramos-breaks-international-win-record|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, ahead of the match against Sweden, Ramos received a plaque from the [[Spanish Football Federation]] to commemorate his record.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/06/ramos-receives-tribute-after-claiming-spain-wins-record|title=Ramos receives tribute after claiming Spain wins record|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=10 June 2019|access-date=10 June 2019|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727064958/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/06/ramos-receives-tribute-after-claiming-spain-wins-record|url-status=live}}</ref> The match ended with a 3–0 win for Spain, where he scored the first goal and extended his tally to 123 international victories.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48589821|title=Spain 3–0 Sweden|work=BBC Sport|date=10 June 2019|access-date=10 June 2019|archive-date=7 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207203649/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48589821|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 September 2019, Ramos scored from a penalty kick his 21st international goal to open the score in Spain's 2–1 away win over [[Romania national football team|Romania]] in a [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying|Euro 2020 qualifier]], which made him the joint 10th top scorer in the history of the national team, alongside [[Míchel (footballer, born 1963)|Míchel]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49574068|title=Romania 1–2 Spain|work=BBC Sport|date=5 September 2019|access-date=5 September 2019|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727061527/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49574068|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 September, Ramos won his 167th cap for Spain in a 4–0 home win over the Faroe Islands in a Euro 2020 qualifier; with this appearance, he equaled Iker Casillas as Spain's most capped player of all time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/09/09/opinion/1568004326_395207.html |title=A couple of goals each for Rodrigo and Alcácer |publisher=as.com |date=9 September 2019 |access-date=11 September 2019 |archive-date=26 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726130432/https://en.as.com/en/2019/09/09/opinion/1568004326_395207.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 12 October 2019, he became the nation's sole [[Spain national football team#Most capped players|most capped]] player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/10/12/football/1570873100_386495.html|title=Sergio Ramos: Spain's history-maker set for record 168th cap|website=as.com|date=12 October 2019|access-date=12 October 2019|archive-date=29 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191029062332/https://en.as.com/en/2019/10/12/football/1570873100_386495.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 September 2020, Ramos scored a brace in a 4–0 win over [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] for the [[2020–21 UEFA Nations League A#Group 4|2020–21 UEFA Nations League]], reaching 23 international goals and equaling [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]] as Spain's eighth-highest all-time goalscorer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54051071|title=Nations League: Ansu Fati, 17, scores for Spain v Ukraine|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=6 September 2020|access-date=6 September 2020|archive-date=10 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200910074225/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54051071|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 November 2020, in a 1–1 draw against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]], he made his 177th appearance for Spain and overtook [[Gianluigi Buffon]]'s [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|record for the most international caps received by a European player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/11/11/ramos-now-leads-europe-as-player-with-most-international-caps|title=Ramos now leads Europe as player with most international caps|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=11 November 2020|access-date=15 November 2020|archive-date=22 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122223038/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2020/11/11/ramos-now-leads-europe-as-player-with-most-international-caps|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ramos made his last international appearance on 31 March 2021 as an 86th-minute substitute in a 3–1 home [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifying]] victory against [[Kosovo national football team|Kosovo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56596747|title=Spain 3–1 Kosovo|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|language=en|date=31 March 2021|access-date=23 February 2023|archive-date=23 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230223175023/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56596747|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2021–2023: Squad exclusions and retirement===
Ramos was excluded from the [[UEFA Euro 2020 squads#Spain|squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2020]], following an injury-plagued season. His omission marked the first major tournament since [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] where he was not called for the national team, ending a run of featuring in ten consecutive tournaments.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sergio Ramos left out of Spain's Euro 2020 squad |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4211736/2021/05/24/sergio-ramos-left-out-of-spains-euro-2020-squad/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=24 May 2021 |date=24 May 2021 |archive-date=25 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210525211200/https://theathletic.com/news/sergio-ramos-spain-euro-2020/jLbJ9jiahxbN |url-status=live }}</ref> In November 2022, he was excluded from the [[2022 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|squad]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ramos, Thiago, De Gea left out of Spain's World Cup 2022 squad|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2022/11/12/no-ramos-thiago-or-de-gea-as-spain-name-young-world-cup-squad|website=Al Jazeera|date=12 November 2022|access-date=5 February 2023|archive-date=5 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205233502/https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2022/11/12/no-ramos-thiago-or-de-gea-as-spain-name-young-world-cup-squad|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ramos announced his retirement from international football on 23 February 2023 at the age of 36, having not appeared for his country in nearly two years, after new coach [[Luis de la Fuente (footballer, born 1961)|Luis de la Fuente]] told him he would no longer be selected.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230223-sergio-ramos-retires-from-spain-duty-after-coach-call |title=Sergio Ramos retires from Spain duty after coach call |publisher=France 24 |date=23 February 2023 |access-date=23 February 2023 |archive-date=23 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230223182528/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230223-sergio-ramos-retires-from-spain-duty-after-coach-call |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Player profile==
===Style of play===
[[File:Sergio Ramos (5275968400).jpg|thumb|right|303px|Ramos has been described as being comfortable on the ball,<ref name="Pedro: Ramos one of the best">{{cite web |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2013/02/13/pedro-ramos-one-of-the-best |title=Pedro: Ramos one of the best |publisher=Football España |date=13 February 2013 |access-date=6 July 2020 |archive-date=27 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201127141902/https://www.football-espana.net/2013/02/13/pedro-ramos-one-of-the-best |url-status=live }}</ref> possessing good technical ability and good [[Cross (association football)|crossing]] ability.<ref name="best player"/><ref name="Sergio Ramos the best defender in the world"/><ref name="best defenders"/><ref name="Ancelotti: Ramos like Maldini">{{cite web|url=http://football-italia.net/50109/ancelotti-ramos-maldini|title=Ancelotti: Ramos like Maldini|publisher=Football Italia|date=5 June 2014|access-date=22 September 2014|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019183850/https://www.football-italia.net/50109/ancelotti-ramos-maldini|url-status=live}}</ref>]]

Ramos is praised for his leadership, athleticism, and his offensive and defense prowess, which allows him to be deployed as a [[centre-back]] and as a [[Full-back (association football)|full-back]]; in his youth, he often played as a right-back, while he later established himself as a centre-back as his career progressed. His former Real Madrid manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]] has compared him to legendary defender [[Paolo Maldini]]; both he and [[Giorgio Chiellini]] called Ramos the best defender in the world.<ref name="A
